## Objective
- Build and continue the complete playable HTML/Canvas 2D shinobi action roguelike, preserving its Part 2 progression systems and completing further master-game phases.

## Requirements
- Maintain a 16:9 landscape shell with a `960 × 540` internal canvas.
- Keep keyboard and mobile touch controls, fixed-step combat, room AI, resources, rewards, progression, and persistent saves.
- Preserve `ashesSave` as the save key and permanent-versus-temporary progression behavior.
- Keep clan, spin, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Rinnegan, Bijuu, and Lee/Guy lineage restrictions intact.

## Decisions
- Continue using the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture rather than replacing it.
- Rinnegan remains separate from normal reward choices and rolls exactly 0.5% after eligible room clears.
- Bijuu are not obtainable through spins and require dedicated boss-defeat or challenge logic.
- Strong Fist and Eight Gates remain exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
- Permanent rewards and unlocks persist; temporary run upgrades reset on death.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the title, 16:9 shell, HUD, progression modal, controls, touch controls, and mobile portrait handling.
- Implemented movement, jumping, attacks, dash, guard/parry, stamina, chakra, enemy AI, projectiles, particles, and wave combat.
- Implemented 11 clans and passives, four independent 20-spin pools, rarity pools, duplicate shards, bloodline restrictions, and ocular ownership restrictions.
- Implemented seven elements with five moves each and nine advanced bloodline types.
- Implemented Sharingan and Byakugan progression restrictions and character identity/customization.
- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, one equipped primary Bijuu, boss arena setup, collection UI, and Bijuu challenge entry.
- Implemented Lee/Guy lineage and Eight Gates availability.
- Implemented permanent identity/progression saves, room rewards, permanent damage/health gains, run chakra restoration, defeat/victory, and restart flows.
- Implemented independent Rinnegan reveal handling and passed `node --check game.js`.

### Active
- Continue Part 3 and any remaining master-game progression work.
- Validate gameplay and progression behavior through local mobile-sized landscape browser testing.

### Blocked
- The Part 3 section of the master prompt was not provided; its exact requirements remain unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Obtain or provide the complete Part 3 prompt before attempting to implement it.
2. Launch the project locally and verify mobile-sized landscape layout, touch controls, combat, menus, and modal flows.
3. Complete and validate any remaining Part 3 systems once their requirements are available.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Main gameplay, progression, combat, rewards, spins, identity, and Bijuu implementation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Title shell, menus, HUD controls, touch controls, modal host.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: 16:9 layout, responsive shell, modal and touch styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: Local launch entry point.

## Important Context
- Local syntax verification passed with `node --check game.js`.
- Browser/mobile verification has not been recorded as completed.
- The project files shown in the recent history remain uncommitted/untracked from Git status; no commit or push has been reported.

MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PART 3 OF 4 — COMPLETE STORY MODE, ROOM MAP, BRANCHING ROUTES, CARD REWARD SYSTEM, SPECIAL DROPS AND BOSSES


This is Part 3 of the same game development project.


Continue using all systems defined in Parts 1 and 2.


This section defines the complete story-mode structure and, most importantly, the reward system.


Do not invent missing progression mechanics. Follow the rules below exactly.


The game must contain eight main story chapters, each with individually designed rooms, explicit connections, branching routes, enemies, hazards, rewards, and boss encounters.


The rooms must feel like interconnected areas of a continuous action roguelike, not isolated combat arenas.


---


26. THE CARD-BASED REWARD SYSTEM — CORE PROGRESSION RULE


EVERY NORMAL SKILL, JUTSU, BUFF, COMBAT MODE, TRANSFORMATION, PASSIVE UPGRADE AND TEMPORARY RUN ABILITY MUST BE OBTAINED THROUGH THE CARD REWARD SYSTEM.


Do not create a separate generic skill-unlock system that bypasses this mechanic.


Do not automatically give the player dozens of combat abilities at the beginning.


The player builds their combat setup by clearing rooms and choosing cards.


This is one of the most important systems in the entire game.


26.1 Basic room-clear reward


After clearing an eligible room:


1. All required enemies must be defeated.
2. The room-clear condition must be confirmed.
3. Combat must stop.
4. The reward interface must appear.
5. The player must receive four card choices.
6. The player must choose exactly one card.
7. The selected card must be added to the player's current run build or permanently unlocked, depending on its card type.
8. The other three choices disappear.


The player cannot select multiple cards from a normal reward screen.


The four cards must appear horizontally.


Each card must display:


- Card artwork.
- Card name.
- Rarity.
- Card category.
- Full effect description.
- Damage, if applicable.
- Chakra cost, if applicable.
- Cooldown, if applicable.
- Duration, if applicable.
- Permanent or temporary status.


The description must clearly explain what the card does.


Do not display vague descriptions such as "Increases power."


Display the exact numerical effect.


26.2 Reward choices based on difficulty


The number of card choices increases with encounter difficulty.


Use these exact initial rules:


Room encounter| Number of card choices
Normal combat room| 4
Treasure room| 4
Challenge room| 5
Elite combat room| 5
Mini-boss room| 6
Main story boss| 7
Optional super-boss| 8


The player still selects only one normal card from the displayed choices.


Special drops are separate and may be awarded in addition to the selected card.


These numbers must be configurable for balancing, but the initial implementation must use them.


26.3 Card categories


Create the following categories:


A. Jutsu Cards


Unlock temporary or permanent-use jutsu for the current run.


Examples:


- Fireball Technique.
- Chidori.
- Water Dragon.
- Shadow Possession.
- Bone Spear.
- Lightning Blade.
- Great Fireball Technique.


B. Skill Cards


Unlock combat abilities and special actions.


Examples:


- Counterattack.
- Chakra Dash.
- Aerial Strike.
- Shadow Step.
- Explosive Kunai.
- Chakra Burst.


C. Buff Cards


Improve attributes.


Examples:


- +15% attack damage.
- +20 maximum health.
- +15 maximum chakra.
- +10% attack speed.
- +12% critical chance.
- +10% movement speed.
- -10% skill cooldown.
- +15% damage resistance.


D. Mode Cards


Unlock temporary combat modes for the current run.


Examples:


- Sharingan Mode, when compatible with the player's clan and unlocks.
- Byakugan Mode, when compatible with the player's clan and unlocks.
- Eight Gates modes, for the Lee/Guy lineage only.
- Bijuu Chakra Modes, when the corresponding Bijuu has been unlocked.
- Other special transformations.


E. Passive Cards


Provide permanent effects for the current run without requiring manual activation.


Examples:


- Increased damage against elites.
- Chakra regeneration improvement.
- Improved parry rewards.
- Increased damage against bosses.
- Reduced damage while airborne.
- Improved weapon speed.


F. Weapon Cards


Provide weapons or weapon upgrades.


Examples:


- Katana.
- Dual Blades.
- Heavy Sword.
- Chakra Blade.
- Special Kunai.
- Unique boss weapons.


G. Ninja Tool Cards


Unlock tools and consumable combat options.


Examples:


- Explosive Tags.
- Smoke Bomb.
- Poison Kunai.
- Shuriken Barrage.
- Special Traps.


H. Support Cards


Provide healing, defensive or utility effects.


Examples:


- Emergency Healing.
- Chakra Recovery.
- Temporary Shield.
- Improved Healing Items.
- Increased Currency Rewards.


All cards must be compatible with the player's character and current progression.


Do not offer a clan-exclusive ability to an incompatible character.


Do not offer Sharingan to a non-Uchiha.


Do not offer Byakugan to a non-Hyuga.


Do not offer Eight Gates to a character outside the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not offer a Bijuu mode if the player has not unlocked the corresponding Bijuu.


26.4 Card rarity


Cards use the rarity system established in Part 2:


- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.
- Mythical.


Higher-rarity cards should generally have stronger or more specialized effects.


Rarity must influence the quality of the options, but it must not make lower-rarity cards useless.


The card selection system must consider:


- Current player build.
- Player clan.
- Equipped element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Available Bijuu.
- Current weapons.
- Previously selected cards.
- Current chapter.
- Encounter difficulty.


Avoid offering four nearly identical cards.


26.5 Card stacking and upgrades


Cards must interact with one another.


Examples:


- Fire damage buff improves Fire Release cards.
- Chakra efficiency improves abilities with chakra costs.
- Critical chance improves fast weapon builds.
- Parry rewards improve defensive builds.
- Weapon-specific upgrades affect the corresponding weapon.


If a player receives a card they already own, the system may:


1. Offer an upgraded version.
2. Improve the existing card's level.
3. Convert it into a defined duplicate compensation effect.


Do not silently waste a card choice.


A card may have multiple upgrade levels.


Example:


Level| Effect
Level 1| +10% Fire damage
Level 2| +20% Fire damage
Level 3| +30% Fire damage


The player must see the new effect before selecting the upgrade.


26.6 Temporary versus permanent cards


Cards must be clearly separated into two groups.


Run Cards:


- Last only during the current run.
- Improve the current build.
- Are removed when the player dies.
- Include most buffs, temporary abilities, temporary weapons and combat modes.


Permanent Unlock Cards:


- Unlock specific permanent content.
- Are saved to the player's account.
- Survive death.
- Must have an explicit permanent-unlock label.


Do not accidentally make ordinary temporary buffs permanent.


Do not accidentally delete permanent unlocks after death.


The permanent progression systems defined in Part 2 remain separate from temporary run builds.


26.7 Reward presentation


The reward screen must:


- Pause normal room combat.
- Display all available choices.
- Use horizontal card placement.
- Clearly show rarity.
- Clearly show card compatibility.
- Allow the player to inspect a card before selecting it.
- Show a selection animation.
- Return control after selection.


Do not generate portrait reward screens.


Do not cover the entire screen with unnecessarily large cards.


Keep the character and environment visible in the background when appropriate.


---


27. SPECIAL DROPS AND UNIQUE BOSS REWARDS


Normal card choices are not the only rewards.


Certain enemies, bosses and special encounters must have their own unique drops.


These rewards must be separate from the normal card selection.


For example, defeating a boss may provide:


- Seven normal card choices, from which the player selects one.
- A chance to receive that boss's signature weapon.
- A chance to receive a signature jutsu.
- Currency.
- A story progression unlock.


Special drops must not replace the normal card choices.


27.1 Signature drop rules


Every major story boss must have a defined special reward table.


Use these initial drop rates:


Drop category| Initial probability
Signature jutsu| 30%
Signature weapon or tool| 20%
Special passive or cosmetic item| 15%


These are separate reward rolls.


If a boss has no suitable weapon or cosmetic, replace that category with an additional thematic reward.


A player may receive more than one special drop from the same boss.


If the player already owns a permanent special item, use a predefined duplicate compensation reward.


Special drops must be recorded in the player's collection.


27.2 Boss signature drops


Implement these reward tables:


Zabuza


- Signature jutsu: Silent Killing Technique.
- Signature weapon: Kubikiribocho.
- Special passive: Hidden Mist Combat.
- Optional cosmetic: Mist Assassin appearance.


Orochimaru


- Signature jutsu: Snake Summoning.
- Signature ability: Hidden Shadow Snake Hands.
- Special passive: Serpent Adaptation.
- Optional cosmetic: Orochimaru-inspired appearance.


Gaara


- Signature jutsu: Sand Coffin.
- Signature jutsu: Sand Burial.
- Special passive: Automatic Sand Defense.
- Optional cosmetic: Sand Guardian aura.


Hidan


- Signature ability: Ritual Curse.
- Signature weapon: Triple-Bladed Scythe.
- Special passive: Ritualist's Resolve.
- Optional cosmetic: Akatsuki-inspired appearance.


Kakuzu


- Signature jutsu: Earth Grudge Fear.
- Signature ability: Masked Elemental Attack.
- Special passive: Hardened Body.
- Optional cosmetic: Elemental Mask effects.


Pain


- Signature jutsu: Shinra Tensei.
- Signature jutsu: Bansho Ten'in.
- Signature ability: Summoning Path.
- Special passive: Six Paths Perception.
- Optional cosmetic: Rinnegan visual effect, only where appropriate.


Madara


- Signature jutsu: Fire Style: Majestic Destroyer Flame.
- Signature weapon: Gunbai.
- Signature ability: Susanoo.
- Special passive: Legendary Shinobi.
- Optional cosmetic: Madara-inspired armor.


Susanoo must respect the character's compatibility and unlock requirements.


Obito


- Signature ability: Kamui.
- Signature jutsu: Wood Release: Cutting Technique.
- Special passive: Dimensional Evasion.
- Optional cosmetic: Masked Shinobi appearance.


Kamui must have clear cooldowns and invulnerability restrictions.


Final dimensional antagonist


- Signature ability: Dimensional Rift.
- Signature jutsu: Advanced Chakra Projection.
- Signature passive: Dimensional Mastery.
- Optional cosmetic: Dimensional Aura.


All signature abilities must have functional animations, hitboxes, cooldowns and resource costs.


Do not simply display them as collectible icons.


27.3 Weapon collection


Unique weapons must have distinct combat behavior.


Examples:


- Kubikiribocho: heavy sword with high damage and slow attacks.
- Gunbai: defensive weapon with special counterattack properties.
- Special chakra blades: faster attacks with chakra effects.
- Unique dual weapons: specialized combo chains.


Weapons must be equipable through the inventory.


---


28. BIJUU ROOM SPECIAL CARD RULE


Each Bijuu has its own special super-boss encounter.


When the player clears that Bijuu's encounter:


1. The player receives eight normal card choices.
2. The game performs a separate 50% probability roll for that Bijuu's corresponding Mode Card.
3. If the roll succeeds, the corresponding Bijuu Mode Card must appear among the eight choices.
4. If the roll fails, it does not appear through that special roll.
5. The other seven or eight choices must follow the normal reward generation rules.
6. The player still selects only one normal card.


The chance must be exactly 50%.


Do not change it according to rarity.


Do not make the 50% chance apply to obtaining the permanent Bijuu Card.


The permanent Bijuu Card is granted by defeating the corresponding Bijuu super-boss, as specified in Part 2.


The 50% chance refers specifically to the corresponding temporary Bijuu Mode Card appearing among the room-clear choices.


If the player already has the permanent Bijuu unlock, the mode card may appear as an available run ability.


If the player has not unlocked the Bijuu, the mode card must not be offered.


28.1 Bijuu mode examples


Each Bijuu must have its own unique mode.


Bijuu| Mode identity
Shukaku| Sand Chakra Mode
Matatabi| Blue Flame Chakra Mode
Isobu| Defensive Shell Mode
Son Goku| Lava Chakra Mode
Kokuo| Boil Chakra Mode
Saiken| Corrosive Chakra Mode
Chomei| Winged Chakra Mode
Gyuki| Tentacle Chakra Mode
Kurama| Nine-Tails Chakra Mode


Each mode must have:


- Activation animation.
- Unique aura.
- Unique transformation appearance.
- Unique stat modifiers.
- Unique abilities.
- Chakra consumption.
- Duration.
- Cooldown or activation restriction.
- Deactivation animation.


Do not reuse one generic transformation with nine different colors.


---


29. COMPLETE STORY MODE STRUCTURE


The main story has eight chapters.


Each chapter contains handcrafted rooms connected through explicit routes.


The player progresses through the rooms by clearing encounters and choosing available exits.


The room map must show:


- Current room.
- Cleared rooms.
- Unvisited rooms.
- Available routes.
- Locked routes.
- Boss rooms.
- Secret rooms.
- Special encounters.


The map must be readable and horizontal.


Do not randomly generate disconnected room graphs.


Use the exact room connections defined below.


Room layouts may have controlled procedural variations, but the room identities, intended connections, and major encounter purposes must remain intact.


---


30. ROOM TYPES AND RULES


Implement these room types.


30.1 Normal Combat Room


Contains standard enemy encounters.


Requirements:


- Defined enemy spawn locations.
- Combat boundaries.
- Clear condition.
- Four card choices after clearing.
- Possible ordinary currency and item drops.


30.2 Elite Combat Room


Contains stronger enemies or special enemy combinations.


Requirements:


- Higher enemy difficulty.
- More complex attack patterns.
- Five card choices.
- Increased currency.
- Better special reward possibilities.


30.3 Treasure Room


Contains:


- Treasure chests.
- Currency.
- Equipment.
- Optional combat challenges.
- Four card choices when the room is cleared.


Treasure rooms must not automatically give every reward.


30.4 Healing Room


Contains a healing station or NPC.


Possible services:


- Restore a portion of health.
- Restore chakra.
- Remove certain negative effects.
- Exchange resources for healing.


Healing must have a defined cost or limitation.


A healing room is a safe room and does not automatically trigger combat.


30.5 Merchant Room


Contains an NPC merchant.


Possible purchases:


- Weapons.
- Ninja tools.
- Healing items.
- Temporary upgrades.
- Card-related services.


Prices must be displayed clearly.


30.6 Challenge Room


Contains a specific combat or movement challenge.


Examples:


- Survive for a set time.
- Defeat enemies without taking damage.
- Defeat enemies before a timer expires.
- Complete a platforming challenge.
- Defeat an elite enemy.


Rewards:


- Five card choices.
- Additional currency or a special item.


30.7 Secret Room


Contains hidden rewards or optional encounters.


Possible rewards:


- Rare cards.
- Special weapons.
- Hidden currency.
- Lore.
- Secret paths.
- Permanent unlock conditions.


Secret rooms must have identifiable discovery methods.


30.8 Story Room


Contains narrative events, NPCs, dialogue or scripted sequences.


Story rooms may include combat, but their primary purpose is advancing the narrative.


30.9 Mini-Boss Room


Contains a stronger named enemy or special enemy encounter.


Rewards:


- Six card choices.
- Increased currency.
- Special drop chance.
- Possible story unlock.


30.10 Main Boss Room


Contains a chapter-ending boss.


Rewards:


- Seven card choices.
- Boss signature reward rolls.
- Chapter completion rewards.
- Story progression.


30.11 Bijuu Challenge Room


Contains one of the nine optional Bijuu super-boss encounters.


Rewards:


- Eight card choices.
- Corresponding permanent Bijuu Card after defeat.
- Separate 50% Bijuu Mode Card appearance roll.
- Unique encounter rewards.


---


31. CHAPTER 1 — THE HIDDEN LEAF


Theme: The beginning of the player's journey, the Hidden Leaf surroundings, forest routes and the first major confrontation.


The chapter introduces basic combat, room exploration, branching paths, treasure, elite enemies and the first boss.

40. ROOM GENERATION AND CONNECTION RULES


The game may use procedural variation, but the main story map must remain handcrafted.


Use reusable room templates for:


- Normal combat.
- Elite combat.
- Treasure.
- Healing.
- Merchant.
- Challenge.
- Secret.
- Story.
- Mini-boss.
- Main boss.
- Bijuu super-boss.


Procedural variation may modify:


- Enemy positions.
- Enemy combinations.
- Small platform arrangements.
- Treasure placement.
- Minor hazards.
- Decorative elements.


Procedural generation must never:


- Remove a required story room.
- Disconnect a route.
- Create an unreachable exit.
- Place a reward outside the playable area.
- Create impossible jumps.
- Make a boss arena inaccessible.
- Replace a named boss.
- Break a required story event.


Every room must have an explicit list of exits and valid destination rooms.


Every route must be tested for reachability.


40.1 Room transition rules


When entering a new room:


1. Load the correct room environment.
2. Position the player at the correct entrance.
3. Set the camera boundaries.
4. Spawn the defined enemies.
5. Activate the encounter logic.
6. Prevent premature exits during active combat.


After clearing the room:


1. Confirm the clear condition.
2. Stop remaining enemy spawns.
3. Display the reward system.
4. Let the player choose a card.
5. Apply the reward.
6. Unlock the next exits.
7. Allow the player to choose the next route.


40.2 Branching route rules


Branching routes must have meaningful differences.


One route may offer:


- More combat.
- Better rewards.
- An elite encounter.


Another route may offer:


- Treasure.
- Healing.
- Exploration.
- A secret encounter.


Routes must reconnect at the exact points specified in the chapter maps.


Do not randomly move the reconnection points.


40.3 Room map interface


The room map must display:


- Room names.
- Room type icons.
- Route connections.
- Cleared status.
- Current position.
- Locked paths.
- Special boss rooms.
- Secret room indicators when discovered.


Use a horizontal map interface.


Do not use a portrait map layout.


---


41. STORY AND ENEMY DESIGN REQUIREMENTS


Every room must have an actual gameplay purpose.


Do not fill the map with empty rooms that exist only to increase playtime.


Each room must contain at least one of the following:


- Combat.
- Exploration.
- Traversal.
- Treasure.
- Healing.
- NPC interaction.
- Story progression.
- Challenge.
- Secret discovery.


Enemy difficulty must increase throughout the chapters.


Suggested progression:


Chapter| Enemy progression
1| Basic rogue ninja
2| Specialized shinobi and dangerous creatures
3| Sand ninja and defensive enemies
4| Akatsuki forces and advanced assassins
5| Invasion forces and summoners
6| Powerful elite shinobi
7| War enemies, reanimated shinobi and large summons
8| Dimensional enemies and final guardians


Do not simply reuse the same enemy with different colors.


Enemies must have different behavior, animations and abilities.


---


42. BOSS DESIGN REQUIREMENTS


Every main boss must be a complete encounter.


A boss must have:


- Unique entrance.
- Dedicated arena.
- Boss health bar.
- Distinct attack patterns.
- Multiple phases.
- Attack telegraphs.
- Unique animations.
- Hit reactions.
- Stagger rules.
- Defeat animation.
- Reward sequence.


A boss should normally have at least two phases.


Major bosses should have three or more phases when appropriate.


Bosses must not be defeated by repeatedly using one basic attack.


The player must recognize patterns and adapt.


42.1 Boss phase changes


Phase changes may be triggered by:


- Health thresholds.
- Scripted story events.
- Specific attack patterns.
- Environmental changes.


During a phase change:


- Show a clear animation.
- Briefly communicate the new threat.
- Change the boss's behavior.
- Introduce new attack patterns.


42.2 Boss fairness


Do not create unavoidable attacks without clear warning.


Every major attack must have a counterplay method:


- Jump.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry, when eligible.
- Movement.
- Positioning.


Some attacks may require more than one of these mechanics.


Do not make every boss attack parryable.


---


43. FINAL REWARD SYSTEM VALIDATION


Before considering the story and progression systems complete, verify every requirement:


1. Every eligible room provides its defined number of card choices.
2. Normal rooms provide four choices.
3. Challenge and elite rooms provide five choices.
4. Mini-bosses provide six choices.
5. Main bosses provide seven choices.
6. Bijuu super-bosses provide eight choices.
7. The player chooses only one normal card per cleared room.
8. Cards include skills, jutsu, buffs, modes, weapons, passives, tools and support abilities.
9. All card effects have complete numerical descriptions.
10. Incompatible clan abilities are never offered.
11. Temporary cards disappear after death.
12. Permanent unlocks survive death.
13. Special boss drops are separate from normal card choices.
14. Bosses have individually defined signature rewards.
15. Each Bijuu has a unique mode.
16. Each Bijuu encounter has an independent 50% chance to include its corresponding Mode Card among the eight choices.
17. The permanent Bijuu Card is still granted after defeating its super-boss.
18. The 50% mode-card roll does not replace the permanent Bijuu Card reward.
19. All eight story chapters exist.
20. Every room listed in this section exists.
21. Every connection follows the specified map.
22. Every branch reconnects at the correct room.
23. Every main boss has a functional multi-phase encounter.
24. Every room has a gameplay purpose.
25. No route creates inaccessible or unreachable content.
26. The room map is horizontal.
27. The reward interface is horizontal.
28. All menus remain landscape-compatible.


Do not treat the room names as sufficient implementation. Every listed room must have its environment, enemy configuration, encounter logic, exits, rewards and gameplay behavior implemented.


END OF PART 3 OF 4.


Continue with Part 4 of the same master document. Preserve all previous systems, room connections, reward rules and progression restrictions.

26. THE CARD-BASED REWARD SYSTEM — CORE PROGRESSION RULE


EVERY NORMAL SKILL, JUTSU, BUFF, COMBAT MODE, TRANSFORMATION, PASSIVE UPGRADE AND TEMPORARY RUN ABILITY MUST BE OBTAINED THROUGH THE CARD REWARD SYSTEM.


Do not create a separate generic skill-unlock system that bypasses this mechanic.


Do not automatically give the player dozens of combat abilities at the beginning.


The player builds their combat setup by clearing rooms and choosing cards.


This is one of the most important systems in the entire game.


26.1 Basic room-clear reward


After clearing an eligible room:


1. All required enemies must be defeated.
2. The room-clear condition must be confirmed.
3. Combat must stop.
4. The reward interface must appear.
5. The player must receive four card choices.
6. The player must choose exactly one card.
7. The selected card must be added to the player's current run build or permanently unlocked, depending on its card type.
8. The other three choices disappear.


The player cannot select multiple cards from a normal reward screen.


The four cards must appear horizontally.


Each card must display:


- Card artwork.
- Card name.
- Rarity.
- Card category.
- Full effect description.
- Damage, if applicable.
- Chakra cost, if applicable.
- Cooldown, if applicable.
- Duration, if applicable.
- Permanent or temporary status.


The description must clearly explain what the card does.


Do not display vague descriptions such as "Increases power."


Display the exact numerical effect.


26.2 Reward choices based on difficulty


The number of card choices increases with encounter difficulty.


Use these exact initial rules:


Room encounter| Number of card choices
Normal combat room| 4
Treasure room| 4
Challenge room| 5
Elite combat room| 5
Mini-boss room| 6
Main story boss| 7
Optional super-boss| 8


The player still selects only one normal card from the displayed choices.


Special drops are separate and may be awarded in addition to the selected card.


These numbers must be configurable for balancing, but the initial implementation must use them.


26.3 Card categories


Create the following categories:


A. Jutsu Cards


Unlock temporary or permanent-use jutsu for the current run.


Examples:


- Fireball Technique.
- Chidori.
- Water Dragon.
- Shadow Possession.
- Bone Spear.
- Lightning Blade.
- Great Fireball Technique.


B. Skill Cards


Unlock combat abilities and special actions.


Examples:


- Counterattack.
- Chakra Dash.
- Aerial Strike.
- Shadow Step.
- Explosive Kunai.
- Chakra Burst.


C. Buff Cards


Improve attributes.


Examples:


- +15% attack damage.
- +20 maximum health.
- +15 maximum chakra.
- +10% attack speed.
- +12% critical chance.
- +10% movement speed.
- -10% skill cooldown.
- +15% damage resistance.


D. Mode Cards


Unlock temporary combat modes for the current run.


Examples:


- Sharingan Mode, when compatible with the player's clan and unlocks.
- Byakugan Mode, when compatible with the player's clan and unlocks.
- Eight Gates modes, for the Lee/Guy lineage only.
- Bijuu Chakra Modes, when the corresponding Bijuu has been unlocked.
- Other special transformations.


E. Passive Cards


Provide permanent effects for the current run without requiring manual activation.


Examples:


- Increased damage against elites.
- Chakra regeneration improvement.
- Improved parry rewards.
- Increased damage against bosses.
- Reduced damage while airborne.
- Improved weapon speed.


F. Weapon Cards


Provide weapons or weapon upgrades.


Examples:


- Katana.
- Dual Blades.
- Heavy Sword.
- Chakra Blade.
- Special Kunai.
- Unique boss weapons.


G. Ninja Tool Cards


Unlock tools and consumable combat options.


Examples:


- Explosive Tags.
- Smoke Bomb.
- Poison Kunai.
- Shuriken Barrage.
- Special Traps.


H. Support Cards


Provide healing, defensive or utility effects.


Examples:


- Emergency Healing.
- Chakra Recovery.
- Temporary Shield.
- Improved Healing Items.
- Increased Currency Rewards.


All cards must be compatible with the player's character and current progression.


Do not offer a clan-exclusive ability to an incompatible character.


Do not offer Sharingan to a non-Uchiha.


Do not offer Byakugan to a non-Hyuga.


Do not offer Eight Gates to a character outside the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not offer a Bijuu mode if the player has not unlocked the corresponding Bijuu.


26.4 Card rarity


Cards use the rarity system established in Part 2:


- Common.
- Uncommon.
- Rare.
- Epic.
- Legendary.
- Mythical.


Higher-rarity cards should generally have stronger or more specialized effects.


Rarity must influence the quality of the options, but it must not make lower-rarity cards useless.


The card selection system must consider:


- Current player build.
- Player clan.
- Equipped element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Available Bijuu.
- Current weapons.
- Previously selected cards.
- Current chapter.
- Encounter difficulty.


Avoid offering four nearly identical cards.


26.5 Card stacking and upgrades


Cards must interact with one another.


Examples:


- Fire damage buff improves Fire Release cards.
- Chakra efficiency improves abilities with chakra costs.
- Critical chance improves fast weapon builds.
- Parry rewards improve defensive builds.
- Weapon-specific upgrades affect the corresponding weapon.


If a player receives a card they already own, the system may:


1. Offer an upgraded version.
2. Improve the existing card's level.
3. Convert it into a defined duplicate compensation effect.


Do not silently waste a card choice.


A card may have multiple upgrade levels.


Example:


Level| Effect
Level 1| +10% Fire damage
Level 2| +20% Fire damage
Level 3| +30% Fire damage


The player must see the new effect before selecting the upgrade.


26.6 Temporary versus permanent cards


Cards must be clearly separated into two groups.


Run Cards:


- Last only during the current run.
- Improve the current build.
- Are removed when the player dies.
- Include most buffs, temporary abilities, temporary weapons and combat modes.


Permanent Unlock Cards:


- Unlock specific permanent content.
- Are saved to the player's account.
- Survive death.
- Must have an explicit permanent-unlock label.


Do not accidentally make ordinary temporary buffs permanent.


Do not accidentally delete permanent unlocks after death.


The permanent progression systems defined in Part 2 remain separate from temporary run builds.


26.7 Reward presentation


The reward screen must:


- Pause normal room combat.
- Display all available choices.
- Use horizontal card placement.
- Clearly show rarity.
- Clearly show card compatibility.
- Allow the player to inspect a card before selecting it.
- Show a selection animation.
- Return control after selection.


Do not generate portrait reward screens.


Do not cover the entire screen with unnecessarily large cards.


Keep the character and environment visible in the background when appropriate.

27. SPECIAL DROPS AND UNIQUE BOSS REWARDS


Normal card choices are not the only rewards.


Certain enemies, bosses and special encounters must have their own unique drops.

---


39. OPTIONAL BIJUU SUPER-BOSS LOCATIONS


The nine Bijuu encounters are separate from the eight mandatory story chapters.


They are optional super-boss challenges.


Each must be accessible through a specific unlock condition or hidden route.


They must not be automatically forced into the main story progression.


Implement these dedicated encounters:


Encounter| Arena theme
Shukaku| Desert destruction arena
Matatabi| Burning blue-flame arena
Isobu| Flooded coastal arena
Son Goku| Volcanic arena
Kokuo| Boiling volcanic battlefield
Saiken| Corrosive marsh arena
Chomei| Floating forest arena
Gyuki| Deep-water battlefield
Kurama| Destroyed village battlefield


Each encounter must contain:


- Dedicated entrance.
- Unique environment.
- Boss health bar.
- Unique attack patterns.
- Multiple phases.
- Arena hazards.
- Distinct music.
- Unique victory sequence.
- Eight card choices.
- Permanent corresponding Bijuu Card after defeat.
- Separate 50% corresponding Bijuu Mode Card appearance roll.


These fights must be among the hardest encounters in the entire game.


They must not be ordinary enemy rooms with increased health.


---


40. ROOM GENERATION AND CONNECTION RULES


The game may use procedural variation, but the main story map must remain handcrafted.


Use reusable room templates for:


- Normal combat.
- Elite combat.
- Treasure.
- Healing.
- Merchant.
- Challenge.
- Secret.
- Story.
- Mini-boss.
- Main boss.
- Bijuu super-boss.


Procedural variation may modify:


- Enemy positions.
- Enemy combinations.
- Small platform arrangements.
- Treasure placement.
- Minor hazards.
- Decorative elements.


Procedural generation must never:


- Remove a required story room.
- Disconnect a route.
- Create an unreachable exit.
- Place a reward outside the playable area.
- Create impossible jumps.
- Make a boss arena inaccessible.
- Replace a named boss.
- Break a required story event.


Every room must have an explicit list of exits and valid destination rooms.


Every route must be tested for reachability.


40.1 Room transition rules


When entering a new room:


1. Load the correct room environment.
2. Position the player at the correct entrance.
3. Set the camera boundaries.
4. Spawn the defined enemies.
5. Activate the encounter logic.
6. Prevent premature exits during active combat.


After clearing the room:


1. Confirm the clear condition.
2. Stop remaining enemy spawns.
3. Display the reward system.
4. Let the player choose a card.
5. Apply the reward.
6. Unlock the next exits.
7. Allow the player to choose the next route.


40.2 Branching route rules


Branching routes must have meaningful differences.


One route may offer:


- More combat.
- Better rewards.
- An elite encounter.


Another route may offer:


- Treasure.
- Healing.
- Exploration.
- A secret encounter.


Routes must reconnect at the exact points specified in the chapter maps.


Do not randomly move the reconnection points.


40.3 Room map interface


The room map must display:


- Room names.
- Room type icons.
- Route connections.
- Cleared status.
- Current position.
- Locked paths.
- Special boss rooms.
- Secret room indicators when discovered.


Use a horizontal map interface.


Do not use a portrait map layout.


---


41. STORY AND ENEMY DESIGN REQUIREMENTS


Every room must have an actual gameplay purpose.


Do not fill the map with empty rooms that exist only to increase playtime.


Each room must contain at least one of the following:


- Combat.
- Exploration.
- Traversal.
- Treasure.
- Healing.
- NPC interaction.
- Story progression.
- Challenge.
- Secret discovery.


Enemy difficulty must increase throughout the chapters.


Suggested progression:


Chapter| Enemy progression
1| Basic rogue ninja
2| Specialized shinobi and dangerous creatures
3| Sand ninja and defensive enemies
4| Akatsuki forces and advanced assassins
5| Invasion forces and summoners
6| Powerful elite shinobi
7| War enemies, reanimated shinobi and large summons
8| Dimensional enemies and final guardians


Do not simply reuse the same enemy with different colors.


Enemies must have different behavior, animations and abilities.


---


42. BOSS DESIGN REQUIREMENTS


Every main boss must be a complete encounter.


A boss must have:


- Unique entrance.
- Dedicated arena.
- Boss health bar.
- Distinct attack patterns.
- Multiple phases.
- Attack telegraphs.
- Unique animations.
- Hit reactions.
- Stagger rules.
- Defeat animation.
- Reward sequence.


A boss should normally have at least two phases.


Major bosses should have three or more phases when appropriate.


Bosses must not be defeated by repeatedly using one basic attack.


The player must recognize patterns and adapt.


42.1 Boss phase changes


Phase changes may be triggered by:


- Health thresholds.
- Scripted story events.
- Specific attack patterns.
- Environmental changes.


During a phase change:


- Show a clear animation.
- Briefly communicate the new threat.
- Change the boss's behavior.
- Introduce new attack patterns.


42.2 Boss fairness


Do not create unavoidable attacks without clear warning.


Every major attack must have a counterplay method:


- Jump.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry, when eligible.
- Movement.
- Positioning.


Some attacks may require more than one of these mechanics.


Do not make every boss attack parryable.


---


43. FINAL REWARD SYSTEM VALIDATION


Before considering the story and progression systems complete, verify every requirement:


1. Every eligible room provides its defined number of card choices.
2. Normal rooms provide four choices.
3. Challenge and elite rooms provide five choices.
4. Mini-bosses provide six choices.
5. Main bosses provide seven choices.
6. Bijuu super-bosses provide eight choices.
7. The player chooses only one normal card per cleared room.
8. Cards include skills, jutsu, buffs, modes, weapons, passives, tools and support abilities.
9. All card effects have complete numerical descriptions.
10. Incompatible clan abilities are never offered.
11. Temporary cards disappear after death.
12. Permanent unlocks survive death.
13. Special boss drops are separate from normal card choices.
14. Bosses have individually defined signature rewards.
15. Each Bijuu has a unique mode.
16. Each Bijuu encounter has an independent 50% chance to include its corresponding Mode Card among the eight choices.
17. The permanent Bijuu Card is still granted after defeating its super-boss.
18. The 50% mode-card roll does not replace the permanent Bijuu Card reward.
19. All eight story chapters exist.
20. Every room listed in this section exists.
21. Every connection follows the specified map.
22. Every branch reconnects at the correct room.
23. Every main boss has a functional multi-phase encounter.
24. Every room has a gameplay purpose.
25. No route creates inaccessible or unreachable content.
26. The room map is horizontal.
27. The reward interface is horizontal.
28. All menus remain landscape-compatible.


Do not treat the room names as sufficient implementation. Every listed room must have its environment, enemy configuration, encounter logic, exits, rewards and gameplay behavior implemented.


END OF PART 3 OF 4.


Continue with Part 4 of the same master document. Preserve all previous systems, room connections, reward rules and progression restrictions.

## Objective
- Build and continue the complete playable HTML/Canvas 2D shinobi action roguelike, preserving Part 2 progression systems and completing further master-game phases.

## Requirements
- Maintain a 16:9 landscape shell with a `960 × 540` internal canvas.
- Keep keyboard and mobile touch controls, fixed-step combat, room AI, resources, rewards, progression, and persistent saves.
- Preserve `ashesSave` as the save key and permanent-versus-temporary progression behavior.
- Keep clan, spin, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Rinnegan, Bijuu, and Lee/Guy lineage restrictions intact.
- Rinnegan remains separate from normal reward choices and rolls exactly 0.5% after eligible room clears.
- Bijuu are not obtainable through spins and require dedicated boss-defeat or challenge logic.
- Strong Fist and Eight Gates remain exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
- Permanent rewards and unlocks persist; temporary run upgrades reset on death.

## Decisions
- Continue using the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture rather than replacing it.
- The complete Part 3 prompt remains unavailable, so no speculative Part 3 systems will be implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the title, 16:9 shell, HUD, progression modal, controls, touch controls, and mobile portrait handling.
- Implemented movement, jumping, attacks, dash, guard/parry, stamina, chakra, enemy AI, projectiles, particles, and wave combat.
- Implemented 11 clans and passives, four independent 20-spin pools, rarity pools, duplicate shards, bloodline restrictions, and ocular ownership restrictions.
- Implemented seven elements with five moves each and nine advanced bloodline types.
- Implemented Sharingan and Byakugan progression restrictions and character identity/customization.
- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, one equipped primary Bijuu, boss arena setup, collection UI, and Bijuu challenge entry.
- Implemented Lee/Guy lineage and Eight Gates availability.
- Implemented permanent identity/progression saves, room rewards, permanent damage/health gains, run chakra restoration, defeat/victory, and restart flows.
- Implemented independent Rinnegan reveal handling.
- Passed `node --check game.js`.
- Confirmed the existing project can be launched with `bash start.sh`.
- Verified the local syntax pass and established that no new behavior was changed after launch.

### Active
- Complete mobile-sized landscape browser testing of layout, touch controls, combat, menus, and modal flows.
- Continue concrete Part 2 verification and remaining master-game progression work once the exact Part 3 requirements are available.

### Blocked
- The Part 3 section of the master prompt was not provided; its exact requirements remain unavailable.
- Browser/mobile visual and gameplay verification has not been completed.

## Next Move
1. Obtain or provide the complete Part 3 prompt.
2. Launch the project locally and verify mobile-sized landscape layout, touch controls, combat, menus, and modal flows.

metadata.displayText:
MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PART 4 OF 4 — VISUAL IDENTITY, CARD ART, ANIMATIONS, CUTSCENES, AUDIO, MENUS, INVENTORY, CUSTOMIZATION, POLISH AND FINAL IMPLEMENTATION


This is the final part of the master game development document.


Continue the same project described in Parts 1, 2 and 3.


Do not replace existing systems or simplify previously specified mechanics.


This section defines the remaining game systems, visual direction, menus, animations, presentation, audio, equipment, character customization and final quality requirements.


The objective is to make the game feel like a complete, polished, responsive, atmospheric action roguelike rather than a collection of unfinished mechanics.


---


44. COMPLETE VISUAL IDENTITY


The entire game must have a consistent pixel-art visual identity.


The visual style must combine:


- Detailed pixel-art environments.
- Fluid character animations.
- Strong silhouettes.
- Atmospheric backgrounds.
- Distinctive character designs.
- Readable combat effects.
- Carefully designed UI.
- Consistent color palettes.
- High-quality environmental details.


Use Dead Cells as a reference for the level of visual polish, animation fluidity, environmental depth and combat readability.


Do not copy Dead Cells characters, sprites, maps, UI or artwork. Create original assets based on the Naruto universe and the game's own visual identity.


44.1 Pixel-art rendering


Use the internal rendering resolution defined in Part 1:


- Internal resolution: 480 × 270.
- Display reference: 1920 × 1080.
- Logical UI resolution: 960 × 540.


Use consistent pixel scaling.


Do not blur pixel-art sprites through inappropriate filtering.


Avoid inconsistent pixel sizes between:


- Characters.
- Enemies.
- Weapons.
- Effects.
- Environment.
- UI icons.


Pixel edges should remain clean.


Use nearest-neighbor scaling where appropriate.


Do not stretch individual sprites.


44.2 Color direction


Each environment must have its own color identity.


Examples:


Environment| Main visual direction
Hidden Leaf| Green, brown, warm natural colors
Forest| Deep green, dark brown, atmospheric shadows
Examination forest| Green, yellow, poisonous purple accents
Desert| Sand, ochre, orange and dark brown
Akatsuki areas| Dark red, black, muted purple
Destroyed village| Grey, dusty brown, smoke and fire
Frozen mountains| Blue, white, pale grey
War battlefield| Dark earth, smoke, orange explosions
Final dimension| Purple, blue, dark grey and unusual lighting
Bijuu arenas| Individual palettes based on each Bijuu


Use lighting and color to reinforce the atmosphere.


Do not make every chapter use the same background colors.


44.3 Environmental depth


Use multiple visual layers.


Every major environment should include:


1. Foreground elements.
2. Playable terrain.
3. Midground structures.
4. Background structures.
5. Distant scenery.
6. Atmospheric effects.


Use parallax scrolling.


Background layers must move at different speeds when the camera scrolls.


The player must remain visually distinct from the environment.


44.4 Environmental animation


The world should feel alive.


Examples:


- Trees moving in the wind.
- Leaves falling.
- Water flowing.
- Smoke drifting.
- Fire flickering.
- Clouds moving.
- Rain falling.
- Snow particles.
- Sandstorms.
- Floating dust.
- Distant lightning.
- Moving shadows.
- Small ambient creatures.


These effects must not interfere with gameplay readability or performance.


44.5 Environmental destruction


Where appropriate, include destructible objects.


Examples:


- Wooden boxes.
- Barrels.
- Small trees.
- Training objects.
- Weak walls.
- Explosive objects.
- Certain boss-arena structures.


Destruction should have appropriate particles and sound effects.


Do not make every environment destructible if it compromises level design or performance.


---


45. CHARACTER SPRITE DESIGN


Every important character must have a recognizable visual identity.


The player, enemies, NPCs and bosses must have different silhouettes.


Do not use the same generic humanoid sprite with different colors for every character.


45.1 Player sprite


The player sprite must support:


- Idle.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Jumping.
- Falling.
- Landing.
- Climbing where applicable.
- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Aerial attacks.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Hit reactions.
- Knockback.
- Skill activation.
- Weapon-specific animations.
- Transformations.
- Death.


45.2 Character readability


Important visual information must remain readable at the internal resolution.


Examples:


- Weapon shape.
- Character silhouette.
- Active transformation.
- Attack direction.
- Defensive stance.
- Enemy telegraph.


Do not make particle effects so large that they hide the character or incoming attacks.


45.3 NPC sprites


Important NPCs must have:


- Unique appearance.
- Idle animation.
- Interaction animation.
- Dialogue portrait where appropriate.
- Recognizable clothing.
- Consistent character design.


---


46. WEAPON-DEPENDENT ANIMATION SYSTEM


The player's attack animations must change depending on the equipped weapon.


Do not use the same punch animation for every weapon.


The equipped weapon must influence the character's:


- Idle pose.
- Movement pose where appropriate.
- Attack animations.
- Combo animations.
- Heavy attack.
- Aerial attacks.
- Dash attack.
- Special weapon attacks.
- Block animation.
- Parry animation.
- Finishing attacks.


46.1 Unarmed combat


When the player has no weapon equipped:


- Use punches.
- Use kicks.
- Use elbow attacks.
- Use physical combinations.
- Use the appropriate clan-specific combat style.


The Lee/Guy lineage must have its own Strong Fist animation set.


46.2 Kunai


Kunai combat must use:


- Short stabbing animations.
- Fast slashes.
- Quick combinations.
- Distinctive kunai idle pose.
- Appropriate weapon hitboxes.


46.3 Katana


Katana combat must use:


- Sword-drawing or ready stance.
- Horizontal slashes.
- Vertical slashes.
- Thrust attacks.
- Distinctive heavy slash.
- Sword-specific parry animation.


46.4 Dual Blades


Dual Blades must use:


- Alternating attacks.
- Faster combinations.
- Two-weapon attack animations.
- Different aerial combinations.
- Distinctive finishing attack.


46.5 Heavy Sword


Heavy Sword must use:


- Slower and heavier swings.
- Strong impact animations.
- Greater recovery.
- Powerful knockback.
- Heavy attack effects.


46.6 Chakra Blade


Chakra Blade must use:


- Chakra-enhanced slashes.
- Energy effects.
- Unique attack trails.
- Special elemental interactions where applicable.


46.7 Staff


Staff combat must use:


- Wide swings.
- Thrusts.
- Rotational attacks.
- Longer-range hitboxes.
- Unique defensive animations.


46.8 Ranged tools


Shuriken, kunai throws and other ranged weapons must have their own animations.


The player must visibly perform the throwing action.


Projectiles must originate from the character's weapon or hand position.


46.9 Weapon switching


When switching weapons:


- Update the character sprite.
- Update the idle pose.
- Update available attacks.
- Update the weapon icon.
- Update the inventory.
- Ensure the new weapon's hitboxes and animations are loaded.


Do not allow the old weapon's attack animations to remain active after switching.


---


47. TRANSFORMATION AND MODE ANIMATIONS


Transformations must visibly change the character.


This applies to:


- Sharingan.
- Byakugan.
- Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eight Gates.
- Bijuu modes.
- Other special combat modes.


Each transformation must have:


- Activation animation.
- Aura or visual effect.
- Character appearance change.
- Unique sound effect.
- Deactivation animation.
- Transformation status indicator.


Examples:


Sharingan:


- Eye activation animation.
- Red eye effect.
- Subtle visual enhancement.


Byakugan:


- Eye activation animation.
- Pale eye appearance.
- Appropriate visual effects.


Eight Gates:


- Increasing aura intensity.
- Progressive appearance changes.
- Stronger movement and attack effects.
- Distinctive activation sequence for higher Gates.


Bijuu Modes:


- Unique chakra aura.
- Different visual appearance for each Bijuu.
- Transformation-specific attacks.
- Appropriate movement and attack animations.


Do not make every transformation a simple color overlay.


---


48. COMPLETE CARD ART AND CARD MODEL SYSTEM


Cards are one of the most important visual elements of the game.


Every card must have an actual visual design.


Do not generate generic cards with only a name and colored rectangle.


Every card must follow a consistent design system while retaining unique artwork.


48.1 Card structure


Each card must contain:


1. Card artwork.
2. Card name.
3. Rarity.
4. Category.
5. Main effect.
6. Numerical effect.
7. Chakra cost, if applicable.
8. Cooldown, if applicable.
9. Duration, if applicable.
10. Compatibility requirements.
11. Upgrade level, if applicable.
12. Permanent or temporary indicator.


The card must be readable on a mobile landscape screen.


48.2 Card dimensions


Use a horizontal reward interface.


Cards should be vertical rectangles placed side by side within the landscape screen.


Reference logical card dimensions:


- Width: approximately 150 units.
- Height: approximately 210 units.


For four-card rewards:


- Display four cards in one horizontal row.
- Keep sufficient spacing.
- Avoid covering the entire game screen.
- Allow the player to inspect each card.


For larger reward counts:


- Six cards: use a balanced horizontal grid or a horizontally scrollable row.
- Seven cards: use a horizontally scrollable row with all seven choices accessible.
- Eight cards: use a horizontally scrollable row with all eight choices accessible.


Do not shrink cards until their descriptions become unreadable.


48.3 Rarity appearance


Use distinct visual treatments.


Rarity| Visual identity
Common| Simple neutral frame
Uncommon| Green frame
Rare| Blue frame
Epic| Purple frame
Legendary| Gold frame
Mythical| Red or special animated frame


Rarity must be immediately recognizable.


Do not make the entire card flash excessively.


Mythical cards may have subtle animated particles or glowing details.


48.4 Card artwork


Every card must use artwork related to its actual effect.


Examples:


- Fireball card: character performing a fire technique.
- Chidori card: lightning gathering around a hand.
- Sharingan card: close-up eye artwork.
- Byakugan card: pale eye activation artwork.
- Katana card: detailed weapon illustration.
- Healing card: healing chakra effect.
- Bijuu Mode card: corresponding Bijuu-inspired transformation artwork.
- Eight Gates card: Lee/Guy-style combat transformation artwork.


Do not use the same artwork for different abilities.

- Compatibility.

- Cooldown.

50. GAME FEEL AND COMBAT POLISH


The game must feel satisfying to play.


This is not optional.


A technically functional attack can still feel bad if the timing, feedback and movement are poor.


Focus on responsiveness and clarity.


50.1 Input responsiveness


- Attacks must activate quickly.
- Movement must respond immediately.
- Button presses must not be lost unnecessarily.
- Jump input must be buffered.
- Defensive actions must be responsive.
- Skill activation must not have unexplained delays.


50.2 Hit feedback


Every successful attack must provide clear feedback.


Include:


- Brief hit pause.
- Appropriate hit effect.
- Impact sound.
- Enemy reaction.
- Knockback where appropriate.
- Damage number or health-bar feedback.


Use short hit pauses rather than freezing the game for too long.


50.3 Screen effects


Use controlled effects:


- Small camera shake on heavy hits.
- Stronger camera shake on major boss attacks.
- Brief impact flashes.
- Subtle slow motion on special finishing attacks.
- Distinctive parry flash.
- Dash afterimages.
- Skill-specific particles.


Provide options to reduce screen shake and visual effects.


50.4 Combat readability


The player must always understand:


- Which enemy is attacking.
- Which direction the attack comes from.
- Whether an attack can be parried.
- Whether the player is in danger.
- Whether a skill is available.
- Whether a cooldown is active.


Avoid visual clutter.


Do not place large effects over incoming attack telegraphs.


50.5 Enemy feedback


Enemies must react to:


- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Parry.
- Dash attacks.
- Elemental effects.
- Critical hits.
- Boss stagger.


Different enemy types must have appropriate resistance.


50.6 Sound and visual synchronization


Every important animation must be synchronized with its sound and hitbox.


Do not make a sword hit before the sword animation reaches the target.


Do not play an impact sound when the attack misses.


Do not allow a projectile to deal damage before it visually reaches the target.
