- Collections.


Every menu button must work.


PHASE 8 — VISUAL AND AUDIO POLISH


Implement:


- Final pixel-art direction.
- Environmental animations.
- Parallax backgrounds.
- Character animation refinement.
- Weapon animation sets.
- Transformation effects.
- Cutscenes.
- Music.
- Sound effects.
- Ambient audio.
- Visual feedback.


PHASE 9 — TESTING AND OPTIMIZATION


Test:


- All screen ratios.
- Landscape orientation.
- Mobile controls.
- Combat.
- Parry timing.
- Dash invulnerability.
- Card rewards.
- Card compatibility.
- Special drops.
- Rinnegan probability.
- Bijuu rewards.
- Save system.
- Room connectivity.
- Boss phases.
- Performance.
- Audio settings.
- UI readability.


Fix bugs before adding unrelated content.


---


67. FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES


These rules apply to the entire project.


1. The game must always be landscape.
2. The game must always use a 2D side-view camera.
3. The gameplay must be a true action roguelike.
4. Combat must be responsive and skill-based.
5. Block and Parry must use the same defensive button.
6. Dash must have limited invulnerability.
7. Every weapon must have appropriate attack animations.
8. All clans must have their defined restrictions.
9. Sharingan and its evolutions are Uchiha-exclusive.
10. Byakugan is Hyuga-exclusive.
11. Rinnegan is an independent 0.5% special reward, never a spin result.
12. Specialized Taijutsu and Eight Gates are Lee/Guy-lineage-exclusive.
13. Bijuu are obtained by defeating their individual super-bosses.
14. There are no Bijuu Spins.
15. There are no universal Taijutsu Spins.
16. Every new player receives 20 spins in each of the four defined categories.
17. All normal skills, jutsu, buffs, modes and run abilities are acquired through the card reward system.
18. Normal cleared rooms provide four card choices.
19. More difficult rooms and bosses provide more choices according to Part 3.
20. The player chooses only one normal card per reward screen.
21. Special drops are separate from normal card choices.
22. Each Bijuu encounter has a separate 50% chance to include its corresponding Mode Card among the reward choices.
23. The permanent Bijuu Card is granted after defeating the corresponding Bijuu.
24. Permanent progression survives death.
25. Temporary run bonuses reset after death.
26. Every story room and route specified in Part 3 must exist.
27. Every major boss must have unique mechanics, animations and rewards.
28. Every important card must have a complete description and functional effect.
29. Menus, inventory, customization and rewards must be landscape.
30. Character appearance must update according to equipped weapons, accessories and transformations.
31. The audio and visual effects must reinforce gameplay rather than obscure it.
32. No major system may be represented by a nonfunctional placeholder.
33. Do not silently remove or simplify requirements.
34. Do not implement systems that contradict earlier parts.
35. Test each system before considering it complete.


---


68. FINAL PROJECT ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST


The project is not considered complete merely because a menu opens or a character can move.


The game must be considered complete only when:


- The player can start a new game.
- The player can create and customize a character.
- The player can use the four spin categories.
- Clan restrictions work correctly.
- The player can enter the village hub.
- The player can select a story mission.
- The player can explore connected rooms.
- The player can fight using weapons and jutsu.
- The player can block, parry and dash.
- Every eligible room provides its correct card rewards.
- Card selection changes the player's actual build.
- Bosses have unique encounters and rewards.
- Bijuu super-bosses work independently.
- The Bijuu reward rules work correctly.
- The eight story chapters are playable.
- The inventory and equipment systems work.
- Weapon-dependent animations work.
- Character customization works.
- Permanent progress saves correctly.
- Temporary run progress resets correctly.
- Audio settings work.
- The pause menu works.
- All important menus work in landscape.
- The game maintains stable performance on Android.


FINAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION:


Build a complete, polished, playable 2D Naruto-inspired action roguelike with the mechanical depth of Dead Cells.


Do not prioritize the appearance of completion over actual functionality.


Every system described across Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 must be implemented as a real, connected, testable game system.


If a feature is too complex to implement immediately, implement it in the specified development order. Do not silently replace it with a simplified placeholder.


Preserve the architecture, progression data, visual identity and gameplay rules across all development phases.


END OF PART 4 OF 4 — END OF MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT.

messages.text:
MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PART 4 OF 4 — VISUAL IDENTITY, CARD ART, ANIMATIONS, CUTSCENES, AUDIO, MENUS, INVENTORY, CUSTOMIZATION, POLISH AND FINAL IMPLEMENTATION


This is the final part of the master game development document.


Continue the same project described in Parts 1, 2 and 3.


Do not replace existing systems or simplify previously specified mechanics.


This section defines the remaining game systems, visual direction, menus, animations, presentation, audio, equipment, character customization and final quality requirements.


The objective is to make the game feel like a complete, polished, responsive, atmospheric action roguelike rather than a collection of unfinished mechanics.


---


44. COMPLETE VISUAL IDENTITY


The entire game must have a consistent pixel-art visual identity.


The visual style must combine:


- Detailed pixel-art environments.
- Fluid character animations.
- Strong silhouettes.
- Atmospheric backgrounds.
- Distinctive character designs.
- Readable combat effects.
- Carefully designed UI.
- Consistent color palettes.
- High-quality environmental details.


Use Dead Cells as a reference for the level of visual polish, animation fluidity, environmental depth and combat readability.


Do not copy Dead Cells characters, sprites, maps, UI or artwork. Create original assets based on the Naruto universe and the game's own visual identity.


44.1 Pixel-art rendering


Use the internal rendering resolution defined in Part 1:


- Internal resolution: 480 × 270.
- Display reference: 1920 × 1080.
- Logical UI resolution: 960 × 540.


Use consistent pixel scaling.


Do not blur pixel-art sprites through inappropriate filtering.


Avoid inconsistent pixel sizes between:


- Characters.
- Enemies.
- Weapons.
- Effects.
- Environment.
- UI icons.


Pixel edges should remain clean.


Use nearest-neighbor scaling where appropriate.


Do not stretch individual sprites.


44.2 Color direction


Each environment must have its own color identity.


Examples:


Environment| Main visual direction
Hidden Leaf| Green, brown, warm natural colors
Forest| Deep green, dark brown, atmospheric shadows
Examination forest| Green, yellow, poisonous purple accents
Desert| Sand, ochre, orange and dark brown
Akatsuki areas| Dark red, black, muted purple
Destroyed village| Grey, dusty brown, smoke and fire
Frozen mountains| Blue, white, pale grey
War battlefield| Dark earth, smoke, orange explosions
Final dimension| Purple, blue, dark grey and unusual lighting
Bijuu arenas| Individual palettes based on each Bijuu


Use lighting and color to reinforce the atmosphere.


Do not make every chapter use the same background colors.


44.3 Environmental depth


Use multiple visual layers.


Every major environment should include:


1. Foreground elements.
2. Playable terrain.
3. Midground structures.
4. Background structures.
5. Distant scenery.
6. Atmospheric effects.


Use parallax scrolling.


Background layers must move at different speeds when the camera scrolls.


The player must remain visually distinct from the environment.


44.4 Environmental animation


The world should feel alive.


Examples:


- Trees moving in the wind.
- Leaves falling.
- Water flowing.
- Smoke drifting.
- Fire flickering.
- Clouds moving.
- Rain falling.
- Snow particles.
- Sandstorms.
- Floating dust.
- Distant lightning.
- Moving shadows.
- Small ambient creatures.


These effects must not interfere with gameplay readability or performance.


44.5 Environmental destruction


Where appropriate, include destructible objects.


Examples:


- Wooden boxes.
- Barrels.
- Small trees.
- Training objects.
- Weak walls.
- Explosive objects.
- Certain boss-arena structures.


Destruction should have appropriate particles and sound effects.


Do not make every environment destructible if it compromises level design or performance.


---


45. CHARACTER SPRITE DESIGN


Every important character must have a recognizable visual identity.


The player, enemies, NPCs and bosses must have different silhouettes.


Do not use the same generic humanoid sprite with different colors for every character.


45.1 Player sprite


The player sprite must support:


- Idle.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Jumping.
- Falling.
- Landing.
- Climbing where applicable.
- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Aerial attacks.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Hit reactions.
- Knockback.
- Skill activation.
- Weapon-specific animations.
- Transformations.
- Death.


45.2 Character readability


Important visual information must remain readable at the internal resolution.


Examples:


- Weapon shape.
- Character silhouette.
- Active transformation.
- Attack direction.
- Defensive stance.
- Enemy telegraph.


Do not make particle effects so large that they hide the character or incoming attacks.


45.3 NPC sprites


Important NPCs must have:


- Unique appearance.
- Idle animation.
- Interaction animation.
- Dialogue portrait where appropriate.
- Recognizable clothing.
- Consistent character design.


---


46. WEAPON-DEPENDENT ANIMATION SYSTEM


The player's attack animations must change depending on the equipped weapon.


Do not use the same punch animation for every weapon.


The equipped weapon must influence the character's:


- Idle pose.
- Movement pose where appropriate.
- Attack animations.
- Combo animations.
- Heavy attack.
- Aerial attacks.
- Dash attack.
- Special weapon attacks.
- Block animation.
- Parry animation.
- Finishing attacks.


46.1 Unarmed combat


When the player has no weapon equipped:


- Use punches.
- Use kicks.
- Use elbow attacks.
- Use physical combinations.
- Use the appropriate clan-specific combat style.


The Lee/Guy lineage must have its own Strong Fist animation set.


46.2 Kunai


Kunai combat must use:


- Short stabbing animations.
- Fast slashes.
- Quick combinations.
- Distinctive kunai idle pose.
- Appropriate weapon hitboxes.


46.3 Katana


Katana combat must use:


- Sword-drawing or ready stance.
- Horizontal slashes.
- Vertical slashes.
- Thrust attacks.
- Distinctive heavy slash.
- Sword-specific parry animation.


46.4 Dual Blades


Dual Blades must use:


- Alternating attacks.
- Faster combinations.
- Two-weapon attack animations.
- Different aerial combinations.
- Distinctive finishing attack.


46.5 Heavy Sword


Heavy Sword must use:


- Slower and heavier swings.
- Strong impact animations.
- Greater recovery.
- Powerful knockback.
- Heavy attack effects.


46.6 Chakra Blade


Chakra Blade must use:


- Chakra-enhanced slashes.
- Energy effects.
- Unique attack trails.
- Special elemental interactions where applicable.


46.7 Staff


Staff combat must use:


- Wide swings.
- Thrusts.
- Rotational attacks.
- Longer-range hitboxes.
- Unique defensive animations.


46.8 Ranged tools


Shuriken, kunai throws and other ranged weapons must have their own animations.


The player must visibly perform the throwing action.


Projectiles must originate from the character's weapon or hand position.


46.9 Weapon switching


When switching weapons:


- Update the character sprite.
- Update the idle pose.
- Update available attacks.
- Update the weapon icon.
- Update the inventory.
- Ensure the new weapon's hitboxes and animations are loaded.


Do not allow the old weapon's attack animations to remain active after switching.


---


47. TRANSFORMATION AND MODE ANIMATIONS


Transformations must visibly change the character.


This applies to:


- Sharingan.
- Byakugan.
- Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eight Gates.
- Bijuu modes.
- Other special combat modes.


Each transformation must have:


- Activation animation.
- Aura or visual effect.
- Character appearance change.
- Unique sound effect.
- Deactivation animation.
- Transformation status indicator.


Examples:


Sharingan:


- Eye activation animation.
- Red eye effect.
- Subtle visual enhancement.


Byakugan:


- Eye activation animation.
- Pale eye appearance.
- Appropriate visual effects.


Eight Gates:


- Increasing aura intensity.
- Progressive appearance changes.
- Stronger movement and attack effects.
- Distinctive activation sequence for higher Gates.


Bijuu Modes:


- Unique chakra aura.
- Different visual appearance for each Bijuu.
- Transformation-specific attacks.
- Appropriate movement and attack animations.


Do not make every transformation a simple color overlay.


---


48. COMPLETE CARD ART AND CARD MODEL SYSTEM


Cards are one of the most important visual elements of the game.


Every card must have an actual visual design.


Do not generate generic cards with only a name and colored rectangle.


Every card must follow a consistent design system while retaining unique artwork.


48.1 Card structure


Each card must contain:


1. Card artwork.
2. Card name.
3. Rarity.
4. Category.
5. Main effect.
6. Numerical effect.
7. Chakra cost, if applicable.
8. Cooldown, if applicable.
9. Duration, if applicable.
10. Compatibility requirements.
11. Upgrade level, if applicable.
12. Permanent or temporary indicator.


The card must be readable on a mobile landscape screen.


48.2 Card dimensions


Use a horizontal reward interface.


Cards should be vertical rectangles placed side by side within the landscape screen.


Reference logical card dimensions:


- Width: approximately 150 units.
- Height: approximately 210 units.


For four-card rewards:


- Display four cards in one horizontal row.
- Keep sufficient spacing.
- Avoid covering the entire game screen.
- Allow the player to inspect each card.


For larger reward counts:


- Six cards: use a balanced horizontal grid or a horizontally scrollable row.
- Seven cards: use a horizontally scrollable row with all seven choices accessible.
- Eight cards: use a horizontally scrollable row with all eight choices accessible.


Do not shrink cards until their descriptions become unreadable.


48.3 Rarity appearance


Use distinct visual treatments.


Rarity| Visual identity
Common| Simple neutral frame
Uncommon| Green frame
Rare| Blue frame
Epic| Purple frame
Legendary| Gold frame
Mythical| Red or special animated frame


Rarity must be immediately recognizable.


Do not make the entire card flash excessively.


Mythical cards may have subtle animated particles or glowing details.


48.4 Card artwork


Every card must use artwork related to its actual effect.


Examples:


- Fireball card: character performing a fire technique.
- Chidori card: lightning gathering around a hand.
- Sharingan card: close-up eye artwork.
- Byakugan card: pale eye activation artwork.
- Katana card: detailed weapon illustration.
- Healing card: healing chakra effect.
- Bijuu Mode card: corresponding Bijuu-inspired transformation artwork.
- Eight Gates card: Lee/Guy-style combat transformation artwork.


Do not use the same artwork for different abilities.


48.5 Exact card descriptions


Create a complete card database.


Every card must have a predefined:


- Name.
- Category.
- Rarity.
- Artwork reference.
- Description.
- Numerical effect.
- Compatibility.
- Chakra cost.
- Cooldown.
- Duration.
- Upgrade levels.
- Reward eligibility.


The game must not invent random descriptions during gameplay.


48.6 Required card examples


The following examples define the expected level of detail.


FIREBALL TECHNIQUE


Category: Jutsu.


Rarity: Common.


Effect: Launches a fireball projectile toward the enemy.


- Damage: 25.
- Chakra cost: 15.
- Cooldown: 4 seconds.
- Range: Medium.
- Can hit multiple enemies if they are aligned.
- Deals Fire damage.


CHIDORI


Category: Jutsu.


Rarity: Epic.


Effect: The player charges forward with concentrated lightning chakra.


- Damage: 55.
- Chakra cost: 35.
- Cooldown: 9 seconds.
- Range: Short to medium.
- Strong single-target damage.
- Can interrupt certain enemy attacks.


PARRY MASTERY


Category: Passive Buff.


Rarity: Rare.


Effect:


- Successful parries restore an additional 5 stamina.
- Successful parries restore an additional 3 chakra.


CHAKRA RESERVE


Category: Buff.


Rarity: Uncommon.


Effect:


- Maximum chakra increases by 15.
- The bonus applies for the current run.


KUBIKIRIBOCHO


Category: Weapon.


Rarity: Legendary.


Effect:


- Unlocks a heavy sword weapon.
- Uses its own attack animation set.
- Base weapon damage: 35.
- Slower attacks.
- Strong knockback.


KURAMA CHAKRA MODE


Category: Mode.


Rarity: Mythical.


Compatibility: Requires permanent Kurama unlock.


Effect:


- Activates a Kurama-inspired chakra transformation.
- Changes the player sprite and aura.
- Grants unique transformation attacks.
- Increases attack power.
- Consumes chakra while active.


All numerical values and restrictions must be stored in the actual card database.


These are examples, not the complete card list.


48.7 Complete card catalog


Create an actual database containing cards for:


- Every base element.
- Every advanced elemental bloodline.
- Every available clan.
- Every available dojutsu.
- Every weapon.
- Every major boss signature ability.
- Every Bijuu mode.
- Every Lee/Guy technique and Gate.
- All buffs.
- All passive effects.
- All ninja tools.
- All healing and support abilities.


Every card must have a complete description and functional effect.


Do not leave categories with placeholder cards.


---


49. CUTSCENES AND CINEMATIC PRESENTATION


Special moments must use short, polished cutscenes.


Cutscenes must enhance the story without interrupting gameplay excessively.


Use original pixel-art animation, character portraits, camera movement, environmental effects and sound design.


Do not use long static dialogue screens for every major event.


49.1 Opening cutscene


Before Chapter 1:


- Show the world.
- Introduce the main conflict.
- Introduce the player character.
- Establish the first mission.
- Transition smoothly into gameplay.


Target duration: 20–40 seconds.


Allow skipping after the first viewing.


49.2 Chapter introduction cutscenes


Each chapter must have a short introduction.


Suggested duration: 8–15 seconds.


Each introduction must show:


- Chapter title.
- Environment.
- Current threat.
- Relevant story objective.


49.3 Chapter boss introductions


Every main boss must have a dedicated entrance sequence.


Examples:


Zabuza:


- Mist spreads through the arena.
- A silhouette appears.
- Zabuza reveals his weapon.
- Boss health bar appears.


Orochimaru:


- A dark, unsettling entrance.
- A short character animation.
- Boss health bar appears.


Gaara:


- Sand begins moving.
- The arena changes.
- Gaara appears with a defensive sand effect.


Hidan:


- Hidan introduces his scythe.
- A short ritual-themed visual.
- Boss encounter begins.


Kakuzu:


- His body and masks are introduced.
- Elemental effects appear.
- Boss encounter begins.


Pain:


- The battlefield becomes quiet.
- Pain enters the arena.
- A short dialogue moment.
- Boss encounter begins.


Madara:


- A dramatic battlefield entrance.
- Strong camera framing.
- Distinctive music transition.


Obito:


- Dimensional distortion.
- A short Kamui visual.
- Boss encounter begins.


Final antagonist:


- Show the final dimension.
- Reveal the boss.
- Begin the final confrontation.


49.4 Bijuu introduction cutscenes


Each Bijuu must have a unique entrance sequence.


Do not reuse the same entrance animation for all nine.


Examples:


- Shukaku rises from the desert.
- Matatabi emerges through blue flames.
- Isobu appears through a massive water surge.
- Son Goku emerges in a volcanic environment.
- Kokuo enters through boiling steam.
- Saiken emerges from a corrosive environment.
- Chomei descends from above.
- Gyuki rises from deep water.
- Kurama appears through a massive chakra manifestation.


These are cinematic descriptions, not substitutes for actual boss mechanics.


Each introduction must establish the creature's scale and identity.


49.5 Transformation cutscenes


Important transformations may have short activation sequences.


Examples:


- First Sharingan activation.
- Mangekyou evolution.
- First Eight Gates activation.
- First Bijuu transformation.
- Major story-related power awakening.


Do not play a long cutscene every time a transformation is activated during combat.


The first activation may use a special cinematic; subsequent activations should be fast and responsive.


49.6 Cutscene controls


All cutscenes must:


- Support skipping.
- Support appropriate subtitles.
- Use correct landscape framing.
- Avoid portrait camera composition.
- Transition smoothly into gameplay.
- Avoid loading delays where possible.


---


50. GAME FEEL AND COMBAT POLISH


The game must feel satisfying to play.


This is not optional.


A technically functional attack can still feel bad if the timing, feedback and movement are poor.


Focus on responsiveness and clarity.


50.1 Input responsiveness


- Attacks must activate quickly.
- Movement must respond immediately.
- Button presses must not be lost unnecessarily.
- Jump input must be buffered.
- Defensive actions must be responsive.
- Skill activation must not have unexplained delays.


50.2 Hit feedback


Every successful attack must provide clear feedback.


Include:


- Brief hit pause.
- Appropriate hit effect.
- Impact sound.
- Enemy reaction.
- Knockback where appropriate.
- Damage number or health-bar feedback.


Use short hit pauses rather than freezing the game for too long.


50.3 Screen effects


Use controlled effects:


- Small camera shake on heavy hits.
- Stronger camera shake on major boss attacks.
- Brief impact flashes.
- Subtle slow motion on special finishing attacks.
- Distinctive parry flash.
- Dash afterimages.
- Skill-specific particles.


Provide options to reduce screen shake and visual effects.


50.4 Combat readability


The player must always understand:


- Which enemy is attacking.
- Which direction the attack comes from.
- Whether an attack can be parried.
- Whether the player is in danger.
- Whether a skill is available.
- Whether a cooldown is active.


Avoid visual clutter.


Do not place large effects over incoming attack telegraphs.


50.5 Enemy feedback


Enemies must react to:


- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Parry.
- Dash attacks.
- Elemental effects.
- Critical hits.
- Boss stagger.


Different enemy types must have appropriate resistance.


50.6 Sound and visual synchronization


Every important animation must be synchronized with its sound and hitbox.


Do not make a sword hit before the sword animation reaches the target.


Do not play an impact sound when the attack misses.


Do not allow a projectile to deal damage before it visually reaches the target.


---


51. AUDIO DESIGN AND MUSIC


The audio system must be fully implemented.


The game must have distinct audio identities for combat, exploration, menus, bosses, transformations and special rewards.


51.1 Music


Create original music inspired by the atmosphere of ninja adventure and action games.


Do not use copyrighted Naruto soundtrack recordings.


Required music categories:


- Main menu music.
- Village hub music.
- Forest exploration music.
- Examination forest music.
- Desert music.
- Akatsuki area music.
- Destroyed village music.
- Frozen mountain music.
- War battlefield music.
- Final dimension music.
- Boss music.
- Bijuu boss music.
- Victory music.
- Defeat music.
- Secret area music.


Music must transition appropriately between areas.


51.2 Boss music


Each major boss should have an appropriate musical identity.


Bijuu should have especially distinctive boss themes.


Music should become more intense during important phases where appropriate.


51.3 Sound effects


Create distinct sounds for:


- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Sword attacks.
- Kunai throws.
- Shuriken throws.
- Parry.
- Block.
- Dash.
- Jump.
- Landing.
- Chakra activation.
- Fire techniques.
- Lightning techniques.
- Water techniques.
- Wind techniques.
- Earth techniques.
- Transformation.
- Healing.
- Card selection.
- Card rarity reveal.
- Weapon pickup.
- Boss entrance.
- Boss phase change.
- Boss defeat.
- Room transition.


Do not reuse one generic sound for every action.


51.4 Environmental audio


Include ambient sounds:


- Wind.
- Rain.
- Water.
- Forest ambience.
- Birds.
- Fire.
- Distant combat.
- Thunder.
- Sandstorms.
- Snowstorms.
- Underground ambience.
- Dimensional environmental effects.


51.5 Audio settings


Allow separate volume controls for:


- Master volume.
- Music.
- Sound effects.
- Ambient sounds.
- Voice and dialogue.


Allow players to mute each category.


Save the settings.


---


52. MAIN MENU


The main menu must use a landscape layout.


It should visually establish the game's identity.


Suggested design:


- Large animated background.
- Player character or important character artwork.
- Atmospheric environment.
- Game title.
- Main menu options arranged horizontally or vertically within a side panel.


Required options:


1. Story Mode.
2. Endless Mode.
3. Boss Rush.
4. Training.
5. Character Customization.
6. Clan Spins.
7. Element Spins.
8. Bloodline Spins.
9. Dojutsu Spins.
10. Inventory.
11. Achievements.
12. Settings.


Do not add Bijuu Spins.


Do not add universal Taijutsu Spins.


The menu must have functional navigation and transitions.


---


53. EXPLORABLE VILLAGE HUB


Create an explorable village hub.


The hub is a safe location where players can prepare before missions.


It must use the same 2D side-view perspective as the main game.


The hub must contain functional NPCs and buildings.


53.1 Hokage / Mission Leader


Functions:


- Story progression.
- Mission selection.
- Main objectives.
- Chapter information.
- Important dialogue.


53.2 Training Instructor


Functions:


- Combat tutorials.
- Practice enemies.
- Movement training.
- Parry training.
- Weapon practice.
- Training challenges.


53.3 Clan Representative


Functions:


- Display clan information.
- Explain clan abilities.
- Show clan-specific progression.
- Display compatibility restrictions.


53.4 Blacksmith


Functions:


- Weapon management.
- Weapon upgrades.
- Weapon appearance.
- Equipment information.


53.5 Mission Administrator


Functions:


- Story missions.
- Optional missions.
- Challenges.
- Endless mode access.
- Boss Rush access.


53.6 Special Unlock Merchant


Functions:


- Exchange appropriate currency.
- Purchase eligible permanent unlocks.
- Purchase cosmetics.
- Display special progression items.


NPCs must have dialogue and working interaction logic.


Do not create decorative NPCs that have no function.


---


54. PAUSE MENU


The pause menu must be available during gameplay.


It must use a horizontal layout.


When opened:


- Pause combat.
- Stop enemy AI.
- Stop timers where appropriate.
- Preserve the current room state.
- Display a clear menu.


Required options:


1. Resume.
2. Current Build.
3. Inventory.
4. Map.
5. Character Status.
6. Settings.
7. Restart Run.
8. Return to Main Menu.


Restart Run and Return to Main Menu must display confirmation dialogs.


The player must not accidentally lose progress through a single misclick.


The pause menu must not allow changing permanent clan or dojutsu restrictions during combat.


It must not allow changing equipped Bijuu or major character identity without the appropriate safe-location restrictions.


---


55. SETTINGS MENU


The settings menu must be fully functional.


It must use a horizontal layout with categories.


55.1 Graphics


Options:


- Pixel scaling.
- Visual effect quality.
- Particle density.
- Screen shake.
- Flash effects.
- Background effects.
- Performance mode.


Do not allow graphics settings to break the pixel-art rendering.


55.2 Audio


Options:


- Master volume.
- Music volume.
- Sound effect volume.
- Ambient volume.
- Voice volume.
- Mute controls.


55.3 Controls


Options:


- Button size.
- Button opacity.
- Button position.
- Joystick sensitivity.
- Button layout reset.
- Vibration.
- Control preview.


55.4 Gameplay


Options:


- Damage numbers.
- Enemy health bars.
- Boss health bars.
- Combat hints.
- Tutorial notifications.
- Screen shake intensity.
- Subtitle settings.
- Auto-pause behavior where appropriate.


55.5 Accessibility


Include:


- Reduced screen shake.
- Reduced flashing effects.
- Adjustable interface opacity.
- Subtitle size.
- High-contrast UI option.
- Alternative visual cues for important attack telegraphs.


All settings must save permanently.


---


56. INVENTORY SYSTEM


The inventory must be a complete functional equipment and collection interface.


Use a landscape layout.


Suggested structure:


- Left: character preview.
- Center: equipment slots and inventory grid.
- Right: selected item details.
- Bottom: equip, unequip, compare and discard actions.


The inventory must contain:


1. Weapons.
2. Secondary weapons.
3. Ninja tools.
4. Accessories.
5. Armor or outfit pieces.
6. Cosmetic items.
7. Special collectibles.
8. Permanent unlock items.
9. Bijuu Cards.
10. Other special progression items.


56.1 Weapon slots


Support:


- Primary weapon.
- Secondary weapon.


When the player equips a weapon:


- Update the character sprite.
- Update the attack animations.
- Update the attack damage.
- Update weapon-specific skills.
- Update the weapon icon.
- Update the inventory status.


56.2 Ninja tool slots


Allow the player to equip appropriate ninja tools.


Examples:


- Kunai.
- Shuriken.
- Explosive Tags.
- Smoke Bombs.
- Poison Kunai.
- Other special tools.


Show available quantity when an item is consumable.


56.3 Equipment comparison


When selecting an item, display its statistics alongside the currently equipped item.


Example:


Attribute| Current weapon| Selected weapon
Damage| 20| 35
Attack speed| 100%| 65%
Range| Medium| Short
Special effect| None| Heavy knockback


Use actual item data.


Do not invent statistics.


56.4 Inventory sorting


Allow sorting by:


- Category.
- Rarity.
- Name.
- Recently obtained.
- Equipped status.


Allow filtering.


Show locked and unavailable items clearly.


---


57. ACCESSORY SYSTEM


Accessories must provide visual customization and, where appropriate, gameplay bonuses.


Possible accessory categories:


- Headbands.
- Masks.
- Shoulder accessories.
- Back accessories.
- Belts.
- Gloves.
- Boots.
- Special aura accessories.
- Cosmetic visual effects.


Accessories must have separate equipment slots.


Suggested slots:


1. Head.
2. Face.
3. Back.
4. Body accessory.
5. Waist.
6. Special visual effect.


Not every accessory must provide a stat bonus.


Separate cosmetic accessories from gameplay equipment.


For accessories that provide gameplay bonuses:


- Display the exact bonus.
- Define compatibility.
- Define rarity.
- Define acquisition method.
- Save the item permanently when it is a permanent unlock.


Accessories must visually attach to the correct character position.


Do not make accessories float or appear disconnected from the sprite.


---


58. CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION


Character customization must be a complete system.


The player must be able to modify their appearance through a dedicated menu.


Use a horizontal interface.


58.1 Appearance options


Include:


- Character name.
- Hairstyle.
- Hair color.
- Skin tone.
- Eye appearance where compatible.
- Outfit.
- Headband.
- Headband symbol.
- Face accessories.
- Back accessories.
- Gloves.
- Boots.
- Cosmetic effects.


58.2 Outfit categories


Examples:


- Standard shinobi outfit.
- Training outfit.
- Dark combat outfit.
- Clan-themed outfit.
- Special mission outfit.
- Event outfit.
- Boss-inspired cosmetic outfits.


Outfits must have consistent sprite designs.


58.3 Clan appearance


The character's appearance may reflect their clan.


Examples:


- Uchiha-inspired visual elements.
- Hyuga-inspired clothing.
- Uzumaki-inspired details.
- Lee/Guy-inspired training outfit.


These are optional cosmetic inspirations and must not force one single appearance on every clan member.


58.4 Appearance preview


The customization screen must include:


- Full character preview.
- Idle animation.
- Running preview.
- Weapon preview.
- Transformation preview when unlocked.


The player must be able to inspect the appearance before confirming.


58.5 Save behavior


Save all customization choices.


Changing appearance must not reset combat progression or permanent unlocks.


---


59. CHARACTER STATUS AND BUILD SCREEN


Create a dedicated character status screen.


Display:


- Health.
- Chakra.
- Stamina.
- Attack damage.
- Defense.
- Movement speed.
- Critical chance.
- Critical damage.
- Chakra regeneration.
- Cooldown modifiers.
- Equipped weapons.
- Equipped accessories.
- Clan.
- Element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Equipped Bijuu.
- Available transformations.


During a run, clearly separate:


- Base permanent statistics.
- Current temporary run bonuses.
- Weapon bonuses.
- Accessory bonuses.
- Active transformation bonuses.


The player must be able to understand exactly where each stat increase comes from.


---


60. ADDITIONAL GAME MODES


Implement the following modes.


60.1 Story Mode


The complete eight-chapter campaign defined in Part 3.


Requirements:


- Story progression.
- Branching routes.
- Boss encounters.
- Permanent unlocks.
- Room rewards.
- Save checkpoints where appropriate.


60.2 Endless Mode


A mode focused on increasingly difficult room progression.


Requirements:


- Endless room sequence.
- Increasing enemy difficulty.
- Increasing elite frequency.
- Periodic boss encounters.
- Card-based rewards.
- Score tracking.
- Survival statistics.


Endless Mode must reuse the card reward system.


Do not create an unrelated progression system.


60.3 Boss Rush


A mode focused on boss encounters.


Requirements:


- Selectable boss challenges.
- Consecutive boss fights.
- Limited healing opportunities.
- Score and completion tracking.
- Rewards based on performance.


Bijuu super-bosses may be included as optional high-difficulty Boss Rush encounters after being unlocked.


60.4 Training Mode


A safe environment for learning combat.


Include:


- Stationary practice target.
- Moving practice target.
- Blocking practice.
- Parry timing practice.
- Dash practice.
- Aerial combat practice.
- Weapon practice.
- Jutsu practice.


Allow the player to inspect damage and cooldown information.


Training Mode must not consume permanent resources.


---


61. ECONOMY AND CURRENCY


The game must have a functional economy.


Use separate currencies where appropriate.


Suggested currencies:


Ryo:


Used for ordinary purchases.


Special Tokens:


Used for rare unlocks and special merchant purchases.


Duplicate Compensation:


Received when duplicate permanent spin results are obtained.


Run Currency:


Collected during a run and used for temporary services or purchases.


Each currency must have:


- Clear icon.
- Displayed amount.
- Acquisition methods.
- Spending methods.
- Save rules.


Run Currency must reset according to the run progression rules.


Permanent currencies must survive death.


Do not create unlimited free purchases.


All item prices must be defined in the item database.


---


62. ACHIEVEMENTS AND COLLECTIONS


Create an achievement system.


Possible achievements:


- Defeat the first boss.
- Complete a chapter.
- Defeat a Bijuu.
- Clear a room without taking damage.
- Perform a perfect parry.
- Defeat an elite enemy.
- Complete a run.
- Unlock a special transformation.
- Obtain a rare weapon.
- Discover a secret room.
- Complete the story.
- Unlock a hidden ending.


Achievements must have:


- Name.
- Description.
- Icon.
- Unlock condition.
- Reward, if applicable.
- Completion status.


Create a collection screen containing:


- Weapons.
- Accessories.
- Cards.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Boss drops.
- Clan unlocks.
- Special cosmetics.
- Achievements.
- Story collectibles.


The player must be able to inspect unlocked and undiscovered items.


---


63. SAVE SYSTEM


Implement a reliable save system.


Save all permanent player data.


This includes:


- Player identity.
- Character appearance.
- Clan.
- Element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Rinnegan unlock.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Equipped Bijuu.
- Taijutsu progression.
- Weapons.
- Accessories.
- Permanent cards.
- Spin counts.
- Obtained spin results.
- Currency.
- Achievements.
- Story progression.
- Settings.
- Control configuration.
- Unlocked modes.


Temporary run data must be saved only if the game explicitly supports continuing an interrupted run.


If not, the game must clearly communicate that temporary run progression is lost when the run ends.


Use safe saving practices.


Avoid losing permanent progression if the game closes unexpectedly.


Do not let a temporary run reset overwrite permanent data.


---


64. PERFORMANCE AND MOBILE OPTIMIZATION


The game must run reliably on Android devices.


Target:


- 60 FPS.
- Landscape orientation.
- Responsive touchscreen controls.
- Stable memory usage.
- Fast room loading.
- Minimal input delay.


Optimization requirements:


- Pool repeated projectiles.
- Pool common particle effects.
- Avoid unnecessary update loops.
- Use efficient collision detection.
- Avoid excessive active enemy counts.
- Optimize background layers.
- Reuse compatible animation resources.
- Avoid loading all chapter assets simultaneously.
- Unload unused room assets when appropriate.


Provide a lower-performance graphics option.


Do not reduce combat responsiveness to improve performance.


---


65. FINAL GAMEPLAY POLISH


The following details are essential for a polished game.


65.1 Room transitions


Transitions must feel smooth.


Use:


- Short fade.
- Door or passage animation.
- Appropriate sound.
- Camera transition.
- Correct player spawn position.


Avoid long black loading screens.


65.2 Rewards


Card rewards must feel satisfying.


Include:


- Card reveal animation.
- Rarity effect.
- Selection feedback.
- Sound effect.
- Clear confirmation.
- Immediate application of the selected effect.


Special drops must have unique reveal sequences.


65.3 Boss victories


When a boss is defeated:


- Stop active combat.
- Play the defeat animation.
- Play a victory sound.
- Display the reward sequence.
- Update the map.
- Unlock the next route.
- Save relevant permanent progression.


65.4 Death and restart


When the player dies:


- Play a clear defeat animation.
- Show the run result screen.
- Display important run statistics.
- Display permanent rewards earned.
- Explain which temporary bonuses were lost.
- Provide Restart Run and Return to Hub options.


Do not make the player wonder what happened to their progression.


65.5 Feedback and responsiveness


Every important interaction must have feedback.


Examples:


- Button press.
- Item selection.
- Equipment change.
- Card selection.
- Purchase.
- Unlock.
- Failed purchase.
- Successful parry.
- Enemy defeat.
- Boss phase transition.
- Transformation activation.


---


66. REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION ORDER


The development AI must implement the project in controlled stages.


Do not attempt to build every system simultaneously.


PHASE 1 — CORE PLAYABLE PROTOTYPE


Implement:


- Landscape orientation.
- Side-view camera.
- Player movement.
- Jump.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Light attack.
- Heavy attack.
- Basic enemy AI.
- Health.
- Chakra.
- Stamina.
- One functional room.


Test all controls on a mobile landscape layout.


PHASE 2 — COMBAT AND EQUIPMENT


Implement:


- Weapon categories.
- Weapon-dependent animations.
- Aerial attacks.
- Enemy variations.
- Damage types.
- Hit reactions.
- Jutsu framework.
- Cooldowns.
- Chakra costs.


Test every weapon and attack.


PHASE 3 — CARD REWARD SYSTEM


Implement:


- Four-card normal rewards.
- Difficulty-based card counts.
- Card database.
- Card categories.
- Rarity.
- Card upgrades.
- Temporary buffs.
- Temporary skills.
- Temporary modes.
- Special drop framework.
- Card selection UI.


Test that selecting a card actually changes gameplay.


PHASE 4 — CHARACTER PROGRESSION


Implement:


- Clans.
- Clan restrictions.
- Elements.
- Bloodlines.
- Dojutsu.
- Spins.
- Rinnegan special reward.
- Lee/Guy lineage.
- Eight Gates.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Permanent save system.


Test all exclusivity restrictions.


PHASE 5 — STORY MAP


Implement:


- Chapter 1.
- Chapter 2.
- Chapter 3.
- Chapter 4.
- Chapter 5.
- Chapter 6.
- Chapter 7.
- Chapter 8.
- Every named room.
- Every branch.
- Every connection.
- Room map.
- Room transition system.


Test every route.


PHASE 6 — BOSSES AND BIJUU


Implement:


- Zabuza.
- Orochimaru.
- Gaara.
- Hidan.
- Kakuzu.
- Pain.
- Madara.
- Obito.
- Final antagonist.
- All nine Bijuu super-bosses.
- Boss signature drops.
- Bijuu Mode Card reward roll.
- Boss animations.
- Boss cutscenes.


Test all boss phases and rewards.


PHASE 7 — HUB, MENUS AND CUSTOMIZATION


Implement:


- Main menu.
- Village hub.
- NPC interactions.
- Inventory.
- Weapons.
- Accessories.
- Character customization.
- Character status.
- Pause menu.
- Settings.
- Achievements.
- Collections.


Every menu button must work.


PHASE 8 — VISUAL AND AUDIO POLISH


Implement:


- Final pixel-art direction.
- Environmental animations.
- Parallax backgrounds.
- Character animation refinement.
- Weapon animation sets.
- Transformation effects.
- Cutscenes.
- Music.
- Sound effects.
- Ambient audio.
- Visual feedback.


PHASE 9 — TESTING AND OPTIMIZATION


Test:


- All screen ratios.
- Landscape orientation.
- Mobile controls.
- Combat.
- Parry timing.
- Dash invulnerability.
- Card rewards.
- Card compatibility.
- Special drops.
- Rinnegan probability.
- Bijuu rewards.
- Save system.
- Room connectivity.
- Boss phases.
- Performance.
- Audio settings.
- UI readability.


Fix bugs before adding unrelated content.


---


67. FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES


These rules apply to the entire project.


1. The game must always be landscape.
2. The game must always use a 2D side-view camera.
3. The gameplay must be a true action roguelike.
4. Combat must be responsive and skill-based.
5. Block and Parry must use the same defensive button.
6. Dash must have limited invulnerability.
7. Every weapon must have appropriate attack animations.
8. All clans must have their defined restrictions.
9. Sharingan and its evolutions are Uchiha-exclusive.
10. Byakugan is Hyuga-exclusive.
11. Rinnegan is an independent 0.5% special reward, never a spin result.
12. Specialized Taijutsu and Eight Gates are Lee/Guy-lineage-exclusive.
13. Bijuu are obtained by defeating their individual super-bosses.
14. There are no Bijuu Spins.
15. There are no universal Taijutsu Spins.
16. Every new player receives 20 spins in each of the four defined categories.
17. All normal skills, jutsu, buffs, modes and run abilities are acquired through the card reward system.
18. Normal cleared rooms provide four card choices.
19. More difficult rooms and bosses provide more choices according to Part 3.
20. The player chooses only one normal card per reward screen.
21. Special drops are separate from normal card choices.
22. Each Bijuu encounter has a separate 50% chance to include its corresponding Mode Card among the reward choices.
23. The permanent Bijuu Card is granted after defeating the corresponding Bijuu.
24. Permanent progression survives death.
25. Temporary run bonuses reset after death.
26. Every story room and route specified in Part 3 must exist.
27. Every major boss must have unique mechanics, animations and rewards.
28. Every important card must have a complete description and functional effect.
29. Menus, inventory, customization and rewards must be landscape.
30. Character appearance must update according to equipped weapons, accessories and transformations.
31. The audio and visual effects must reinforce gameplay rather than obscure it.
32. No major system may be represented by a nonfunctional placeholder.
33. Do not silently remove or simplify requirements.
34. Do not implement systems that contradict earlier parts.
35. Test each system before considering it complete.


---


68. FINAL PROJECT ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST


The project is not considered complete merely because a menu opens or a character can move.


The game must be considered complete only when:


- The player can start a new game.
- The player can create and customize a character.
- The player can use the four spin categories.
- Clan restrictions work correctly.
- The player can enter the village hub.
- The player can select a story mission.
- The player can explore connected rooms.
- The player can fight using weapons and jutsu.
- The player can block, parry and dash.
- Every eligible room provides its correct card rewards.
- Card selection changes the player's actual build.
- Bosses have unique encounters and rewards.
- Bijuu super-bosses work independently.
- The Bijuu reward rules work correctly.
- The eight story chapters are playable.
- The inventory and equipment systems work.
- Weapon-dependent animations work.
- Character customization works.
- Permanent progress saves correctly.
- Temporary run progress resets correctly.
- Audio settings work.
- The pause menu works.
- All important menus work in landscape.
- The game maintains stable performance on Android.


FINAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION:


Build a complete, polished, playable 2D Naruto-inspired action roguelike with the mechanical depth of Dead Cells.


Do not prioritize the appearance of completion over actual functionality.


Every system described across Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 must be implemented as a real, connected, testable game system.


If a feature is too complex to implement immediately, implement it in the specified development order. Do not silently replace it with a simplified placeholder.


Preserve the architecture, progression data, visual identity and gameplay rules across all development phases.


END OF PART 4 OF 4 — END OF MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT DOCUMENT.

## Objective
- Build and continue the complete playable HTML/Canvas 2D shinobi action roguelike, including chapter routing, room traversal, card rewards, boss drops, Bijuu encounters, progression, and hidden-ending systems.

## Requirements
- Preserve the `960 × 540` 16:9 Canvas shell, keyboard/mobile controls, fixed-step combat, saves using the `ashesSave` key, and permanent-versus-run progression separation.
- Implement eight chapters, branching room routes, reconnections, bosses, encounters, hazards, merchants, secrets, and 77+ rooms.
- Use exact horizontal reward counts of 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8 cards and require exactly one choice per eligible room.
- Keep Rinnegan separate with exactly 0.5% after eligible room clears.
- Keep Bijuu permanent unlocks separate from spins, with dedicated defeats and exact 50% temporary Mode Card rolls.
- Preserve clan, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Lee/Guy gates, Rinnegan, weapon, and lineage restrictions.
- Implement boss signature drops, weapon collection/equip behavior, hidden-ending objectives, and horizontal landscape-compatible menus.

## Decisions
- Continue using the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture.
- Permanent progression and temporary run builds remain separate.
- Rinnegan reveal handling remains independent of ordinary rewards.
- A compact Chapter 1–8 route framework is currently the implementation bridge until exact Part 3 room specifications are available.
- Do not introduce speculative Part 4 systems.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title shell, HUD, progression modal, controls, mobile touch controls, portrait handling, and 16:9 styling.
- Implemented fixed-step movement, combat, AI, projectiles, particles, resources, saves, and defeat/victory flows.
- Implemented clans, permanent spin pools, rarity rolls, duplicate shards, bloodline/ocular restrictions, Sharingan, Byakugan, elements, bloodlines, Lee/Guy gates, and weapon-related progression.
- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, Bijuu challenges, permanent Bijuu equipment, and primary Bijuu behavior.
- Implemented permanent identity/progression saves, reset behavior for temporary run cards, and independent Rinnegan unlock handling.
- Added a deterministic Chapter 1–8 route framework, story chapter names, room indexing, count-specific story reward generation, and horizontal route/map UI hooks.
- Added `STORY_CHAPTERS`, `storyRewardOptions`, `applyRunReward`, `startStoryRoom`, `showChapterMap`, `completeStoryRoom`, and `finishRoomChoice`.
- Added compact room routing into `initRun` and reconcile-facing story-clear logic scaffolding.
- Passed `node --check game.js` in earlier work.

### Active
- Replace the legacy three-wave clear flow completely with story-room completion and reconnection traversal.
- Replace the old fixed reward presentation with exact 3/4/5/6/7/8-card horizontal choices and exactly-one-selection enforcement.
- Integrate the existing update and enemy-clear logic with the newly added story room state.
- Add exact Part 3 room maps and room types, reconnections, hazards, merchants, healing, treasure, challenges, and secrets.
- Add functional boss phases and signature boss drops.
- Add dedicated Bijuu defeat completion and exact 50% temporary Mode Card rolls.
- Perform desktop and mobile landscape verification.

### Blocked
- Exact Part 3 room graph and boss/drop tables remain unavailable.
- Browser/mobile visual and gameplay testing remains incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Patch the exact enemy-clear branch in `game.js` to call `completeStoryRoom()` for every story room instead of the legacy wave/reward branch.
2. Replace `showRewards()` with the exact-count `storyRewardOptions()` presentation and one-selection-only behavior.
3. Keep 0.5% Rinnegan handling separate from all ordinary reward choices.
4. Implement the 77+ room data, reconnections, environments, hazards, merchants, secrets, and exit locking.
5. Implement boss phases, signature weapon drops, equip/collection behavior, Bijuu rewards, and hidden-ending objectives.
6. Run `node --check game.js`, launch the game, and verify desktop and mobile landscape layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Main gameplay, combat, saves, story routing, rewards, bosses, and Bijuu implementation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Canvas shell, title, HUD, modal, and touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: 16:9 shell, route/reward modals, and mobile landscape styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: Local launch entry point.

## Important Context
- Current project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- The `ashesSave` key remains the persistence identifier.
- The compact Chapter 1–8 implementation currently coexists with the legacy wave loop and has not yet fully reconciled it.
- Permanent unlocks survive defeat; temporary run cards and upgrades must reset on death.
- Rinnegan and Bijuu rewards must not be exposed through clan, element, bloodline, or dojutsu spins.
- The exact full Part 3 specification and exact Part 4 specification were not present in the available source context.

## Objective
- Complete a polished, playable HTML/Canvas 2D Naruto-inspired action roguelike with Part 4 menus, progression, inventory, customization, audio, additional modes, and final presentation.

## Requirements
- Preserve `960 × 540` logical resolution, 16:9 shell, mobile controls, fixed-step combat, `ashesSave` persistence, and 480 × 270 internal rendering.
- Keep permanent progression separate from temporary run cards and upgrades.
- Preserve exact 3/4/5/6/7/8-card horizontal rewards, one selection per eligible room, independent 0.5% Rinnegan rewards, Bijuu unlocks, and exact 50% Bijuu Mode Card rolls.
- Preserve clan, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Lee/Guy gate, weapon, and lineage restrictions.
- Preserve 2D side-view gameplay, landscape-only layouts, and the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture.
- Implement inventory, equipment, customization, settings, hub, achievements, collection interfaces, and additional modes without speculative systems.

## Decisions
- Permanent progression and temporary run builds remain separate.
- Rinnegan remains independent from ordinary reward and permanent spin pools.
- Bijuu permanent unlocks remain separate from temporary card rolls.
- The compact Chapter 1–8 routing framework remains the implementation bridge until exact Part 3 room graphs are available.
- Story rooms now use exact-count reward selection rather than the legacy wave/reward flow.
- The run-card database is represented by `RUN_CARD_DB`, and `storyRewardOptions(count)` shuffles it and returns exactly `count` distinct cards when enough cards exist.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented title shell, 16:9 presentation, HUD, progression modal, controls, portrait handling, mobile touch controls, and settings-oriented UI structure.
- Implemented fixed-step movement, combat, AI, projectiles, particles, resources, saves, defeat/victory, and fixed-step update behavior.
- Implemented clans, permanent spin pools, rarity rolls, duplicate shards, bloodline and ocular restrictions, Sharingan, Byakugan, elements, Lee/Guy gates, weapons, and lineage progression.
- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, Bijuu challenges, permanent Bijuu equipment, and primary Bijuu behavior.
- Implemented permanent identity saves and temporary-run reset behavior.
- Added deterministic Chapter 1–8 routing, room indexing, story reward generation, compact story-room routing, and chapter-map hooks.
- Added `STORY_CHAPTERS`, `storyRewardOptions`, `applyRunReward`, `startStoryRoom`, `showChapterMap`, `completeStoryRoom`, and `finishRoomChoice`.
- Replaced the legacy reward option pool with a structured, distinct-card `RUN_CARD_DB` presentation layer.
- Passed `node --check game.js`.

### Active
- Replace legacy wave/reward clearing completely with `completeStoryRoom()` for every story room.
- Enforce exactly one reward selection per eligible room and retain Rinnegan reveal handling outside ordinary rewards.
- Integrate story clearing with existing enemy-clear and update logic.
- Implement complete inventory/equipment, weapon switching, customization, settings/audio, hub NPC logic, achievements, and collection interfaces.
- Implement additional game modes and final presentation polish.

### Blocked
- Exact full Part 3 room graphs and boss/drop tables remain unavailable.
- Desktop and mobile landscape gameplay verification remains incomplete.
- Exact boss phases, signature drops, dedicated Bijuu cutscenes, and 77+ room details cannot be finalized without exact specifications.

## Next Move
1. Patch the enemy-clear branch to call `completeStoryRoom()` for every story room instead of the legacy wave/reward branch.
2. Replace `showRewards()` with exact-count `storyRewardOptions()` presentation and enforce one-selection completion.
3. Keep Rinnegan reveal handling separate from ordinary cards.
4. Complete inventory, permanent/temporary equipment separation, customization, settings/audio, hub, achievements, and collection interfaces.
5. Implement additional modes and presentation/combat polish.
6. Add exact routing, reconnections, environments, hazards, merchants, healing, treasure, challenges, and secrets once specifications are available.
7. Run `node --check game.js`, launch the game, and verify desktop and mobile landscape layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Main combat, routing, cards, inventory, progression, bosses, modes, saves, and menus.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Canvas shell, title, HUD, modal, and mobile controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: 16:9 shell, reward/card presentation, responsive layout, and mobile styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: Local launch entry point.

## Important Context
- Existing project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- Normal story-cleared rooms require 4 choices; difficult rooms and bosses use Part 3-defined 3/5/6/7/8 counts.
- Temporary run progress and permanent unlocks must never overwrite each other.
- Independent Rinnegan handling must not be merged into ordinary reward or spin pools.
- Bijuu unlock and Bijuu Mode roll behavior must remain separate and preserve 50% Bijuu Mode Card rolls.
- Final Part 3 room data and boss specifications remain pending.
