metadata.displayText:
PART 5 — COMPLETE CARD SYSTEM, CARD RARITY, DROP RATES, PROGRESSION AND MODE EVOLUTION

1. CORE CARD SYSTEM — NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE


Cards are the central progression and build-customization system of the entire game.


The player must obtain skills, passive abilities, stat upgrades, weapons, transformations, mode evolutions, and special enhancements through cards.


Do NOT create a separate generic skill-unlock system that bypasses cards.


Do NOT automatically grant fully upgraded abilities or transformations when the player first unlocks them.


Every card must have a clearly defined purpose, rarity, effect, compatibility requirement, progression stage, and acquisition method.


There are two main types of card progression:


1. Permanent Cards: Permanently unlock a skill, ability, weapon, mode, or progression upgrade. Once obtained, they remain in the player's collection.
2. Run Cards: Provide temporary bonuses during the current run. They are lost when the run ends or the player dies, unless a specific permanent effect says otherwise.


Some permanent abilities require multiple additional cards to reach their full potential. Unlocking the base ability does NOT automatically unlock every upgrade.


---


2. CARD CATEGORIES


Organize the card collection into the following categories:


A. Active Skill Cards


Unlock abilities that the player can actively use during combat.


Examples:


- Fireball Jutsu
- Chidori
- Rasengan
- Shadow Clone Jutsu
- Substitution Technique
- Gentle Fist
- Rotation
- Lightning-based attacks
- Weapon techniques
- Clan-exclusive abilities


Each active skill card must define:


- Skill name
- Skill description
- Card rarity
- Chakra cost
- Cooldown
- Damage
- Range
- Area of effect
- Startup time
- Recovery time
- Upgrade possibilities
- Clan, element, bloodline, or mode requirements
- Whether the skill is permanent or temporary


B. Passive Ability Cards


Provide permanent or temporary passive effects.


Examples:


- Increased maximum health
- Increased maximum chakra
- Increased stamina
- Faster chakra regeneration
- Increased critical-hit chance
- Increased critical-hit damage
- Reduced cooldowns
- Increased movement speed
- Increased weapon damage
- Increased resistance to specific elements
- Improved healing effects
- Improved parry recovery


Passive cards must have balanced values and clear descriptions.


C. Stat Upgrade Cards


Directly improve player statistics.


Examples:


- Vitality: +10 maximum health.
- Chakra Reserve: +10 maximum chakra.
- Stamina Training: +10 maximum stamina.
- Focus: +5% skill damage.
- Weapon Mastery: +5% weapon damage.
- Quick Recovery: +5% cooldown recovery speed.


These cards may have multiple upgrade levels.


Do not allow unlimited stacking of the same bonus without a defined maximum.


D. Weapon Cards


Unlock weapons or weapon-related improvements.


Examples:


- Kunai Mastery
- Katana Mastery
- Dual Blade Mastery
- Heavy Sword Mastery
- Chakra Blade Mastery
- Staff Mastery
- Shuriken Mastery
- Special Boss Weapons


Some weapons must be obtained through specific boss drops rather than ordinary random card rewards.


E. Mode Cards


These cards progressively unlock and improve special modes.


Examples:


- Sharingan Activation
- Sharingan Mastery
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan
- Mangekyou Sharingan
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan
- Byakugan Mastery
- Eight Gates progression
- Bijuu Chakra Control
- Bijuu Transformation Stages
- Kurama Chakra Control


Mode Cards are especially important and must follow the progressive evolution system described later in this document.


F. Run Enhancement Cards


These cards provide temporary effects for the current run.


Examples:


- +20% damage for the current run.
- +15% maximum health for the current run.
- +10% movement speed for the current run.
- +20% chakra regeneration for the current run.
- +10% critical-hit chance for the current run.
- Reduced cooldowns for the current run.


Run Enhancement Cards must be clearly marked as temporary.


---


3. CARD RARITY SYSTEM


Every card has one of six rarities.


Use these exact base rarity probabilities for the rarity roll:


Rarity| Base Probability
Common| 50%
Uncommon| 25%
Rare| 15%
Epic| 7%
Legendary| 2.5%
Mythical| 0.5%


These probabilities represent the base rarity distribution, not the chance of receiving a specific named card.


The game must perform the rarity roll first, then select an eligible card from that rarity's pool.


A card's rarity determines its potential power, complexity, and uniqueness, but rarity alone must not make a card useless or automatically superior in every situation.


COMMON


- Basic and accessible effects.
- Small stat improvements.
- Basic combat skills.
- Early progression cards.
- Simple weapon improvements.


Examples:


- +5 maximum health.
- +5 maximum chakra.
- Basic Kunai Mastery.
- Small movement-speed increase.
- Basic Fireball improvement.


UNCOMMON


- Improved versions of basic abilities.
- Moderate stat improvements.
- Basic combinations of effects.
- Additional utility.


Examples:


- +10 maximum health.
- +5% weapon damage.
- Improved Fireball damage.
- Faster stamina recovery.
- Improved basic combo damage.


RARE


- Strong combat improvements.
- More specialized abilities.
- Meaningful upgrades to existing skills.
- More powerful passive effects.


Examples:


- Chidori enhancement.
- Improved Shadow Clone Jutsu.
- Increased critical-hit chance.
- Improved dash recovery.
- Sharingan perception enhancement.


EPIC


- Powerful abilities and advanced upgrades.
- Special combat mechanics.
- Major improvements to existing modes.
- Strong combinations of effects.


Examples:


- Advanced Chidori.
- Mangekyou progression card.
- Advanced Byakugan perception.
- Eight Gates advancement.
- Powerful weapon techniques.


LEGENDARY


- Extremely powerful and specialized cards.
- Unique abilities.
- Major transformation improvements.
- Rare boss-related abilities.
- High-impact permanent upgrades.


Examples:


- Susanoo progression card.
- Advanced Bijuu Chakra Control.
- Eight Gates higher-stage progression.
- Powerful signature boss techniques.
- Advanced transformation mastery.


MYTHICAL


- Extremely rare, exceptional cards.
- Unique or highly specialized effects.
- Major milestones in progression.
- Special abilities that significantly change a build.


Examples:


- Eternal Mangekyou progression.
- Advanced Bijuu transformation evolution.
- Extremely rare unique techniques.
- Special high-level mode enhancements.


Mythical cards must remain exceptionally rare. Do not fill the ordinary card pool with mythical cards just to make rewards feel more exciting.


---


4. CARD DROP PROBABILITIES AND REWARD RULES


Every room must follow the established reward-choice system.


Standard Room


After clearing a standard room:


- Generate exactly 4 card choices.
- The player selects exactly 1 card.
- The other choices disappear.
- The selected card is added to the player's collection or current run, depending on its type.


Elite and Difficult Rooms


Harder rooms must provide additional choices and better reward quality.


Use this progression:


- Standard Room: 4 choices.
- Elite Room: 5 choices.
- Mini-Boss Room: 6 choices.
- Main Boss Room: 7 choices.
- Optional Bijuu Challenge: 8 choices.


Higher difficulty should improve the reward quality and may increase the probability of higher rarities, without making powerful cards guaranteed.


Rarity Scaling by Progression


The rarity probabilities must evolve as the player advances through the story.


Use the following base progression:


Early Game — Chapter 1


- Common: 65%
- Uncommon: 25%
- Rare: 8%
- Epic: 1.8%
- Legendary: 0.19%
- Mythical: 0.01%


Early-Mid Game — Chapters 2–3


- Common: 55%
- Uncommon: 27%
- Rare: 13%
- Epic: 4%
- Legendary: 0.9%
- Mythical: 0.1%


Mid Game — Chapters 4–5


- Common: 45%
- Uncommon: 28%
- Rare: 17%
- Epic: 7%
- Legendary: 2.5%
- Mythical: 0.5%


Late Game — Chapters 6–7


- Common: 35%
- Uncommon: 28%
- Rare: 20%
- Epic: 10%
- Legendary: 5.5%
- Mythical: 1.5%


Final Chapter — Chapter 8


- Common: 30%
- Uncommon: 25%
- Rare: 22%
- Epic: 13%
- Legendary: 7.5%
- Mythical: 2.5%


Each progression table totals 100%.


These probabilities determine the rarity of each generated card choice. The game must still generate the correct number of choices for the room.


The card pool must also be restricted by progression. A player in Chapter 1 must not receive endgame abilities simply because a high rarity was rolled.


A Legendary card can only appear when its specific progression requirements are met.


A Mythical card can only appear when its specific progression requirements are met.


The game must use both:


1. Rarity probability.
2. Card eligibility based on chapter, unlocks, character compatibility, and progression.


A high rarity roll does not override eligibility restrictions.


Important Reward Separation


Special rewards must not silently replace ordinary card choices.


The following systems are independent:


- Ordinary card reward generation.
- Specific boss signature drops.
- Guaranteed permanent Bijuu card rewards.
- The 50% Bijuu Mode Card appearance chance.
- The independent 0.5% Rinnegan reward chance.


Each system must be processed separately and clearly.


---


5. WHEN EACH CARD CAN FIRST APPEAR


Every card must have a minimum chapter or unlock requirement.


Use these general progression rules:


Chapter 1 — Basic Foundation


Available cards:


- Basic weapon cards.
- Basic combat abilities.
- Basic elemental abilities.
- Basic health, chakra, and stamina upgrades.
- Basic movement and defense upgrades.
- Common and Uncommon cards.
- A limited selection of Rare cards.


Do not allow advanced transformations or endgame abilities to appear.


Chapters 2–3 — Intermediate Abilities


Introduce:


- More advanced elemental jutsu.
- Clan-specific abilities.
- Weapon specialization.
- Improved combat passives.
- Basic bloodline abilities.
- Early stages of eligible dojutsu progression.
- More Rare and Epic cards.


Chapters 4–5 — Advanced Combat


Introduce:


- Advanced clan abilities.
- Stronger elemental techniques.
- Advanced bloodline abilities.
- More powerful dojutsu progression cards.
- Advanced weapon techniques.
- Early high-level transformation improvements.
- Legendary cards with appropriate unlock requirements.


Chapters 6–7 — High-Level Progression


Introduce:


- Advanced dojutsu upgrades.
- Powerful clan techniques.
- Advanced transformations.
- High-level Bijuu progression cards, if the player already owns the corresponding Bijuu.
- Rare signature boss techniques.
- More Legendary and Mythical cards.


Chapter 8 — Endgame


Introduce:


- Final-stage progression cards.
- Highest-level transformation improvements.
- Extremely powerful special abilities.
- Endgame passive upgrades.
- Mythical cards with strict requirements.


These are minimum progression guidelines. Individual cards must have their own specific unlock conditions.


A card must never appear if the player cannot use it and has no valid path to unlock it.


---


6. DUPLICATE CARDS AND CARD COLLECTION


When the player receives a card they already own:


- If it is a permanent card with upgrade levels, allow the duplicate to contribute toward its next upgrade when applicable.
- If the card is already at maximum level, convert it into Duplicate Compensation.
- If it is a temporary Run Card, handle duplicates according to its stacking rules.
- Never silently delete a duplicate without giving the player a defined result.


The collection interface must display:


- Card name.
- Card artwork.
- Rarity.
- Current level.
- Maximum level.
- Effect.
- Upgrade requirements.
- Acquisition source.
- Compatibility requirements.
- Whether the card is permanent or temporary.


The player must be able to inspect locked cards and see their unlock conditions.


---


7. PROGRESSIVE MODE EVOLUTION — EXTREMELY IMPORTANT


Special modes must NOT be fully unlocked when the player obtains their first related card.


The player must progressively develop each mode by collecting specific Mode Cards.


The first card should unlock the initial functionality, not the complete transformation.


Additional cards unlock new stages, improve control, increase effectiveness, and grant new abilities.


This applies to:


- Sharingan.
- Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Byakugan.
- Eight Gates.
- Bijuu modes.
- Other advanced transformations.


Each mode must have a progression tree with clear stages and requirements.


The player must be able to see:


- Current mode stage.
- Next available stage.
- Required cards.
- Current bonuses.
- New abilities unlocked by each stage.
- Chakra or stamina costs.
- Transformation duration or limitations.
- Visual appearance of each stage.


Do not automatically unlock all stages after obtaining the first card.


---


8. SHARINGAN PROGRESSION


Sharingan is exclusive to the Uchiha clan.


A non-Uchiha character must never obtain Sharingan through ordinary cards, spins, or random rewards.


The player must progressively evolve the Sharingan through Mode Cards.


Stage 1 — Sharingan Activation


Required card: Sharingan Activation.


Unlocks:


- Basic Sharingan activation.
- Red eye appearance with one tomoe.
- Slightly improved enemy movement perception.
- Small reaction-time improvement.
- Basic chakra perception.


This is only the initial Sharingan stage.


Stage 2 — Two-Tomoe Sharingan


Required card: Two-Tomoe Mastery.


Unlocks:


- Two-tomoe appearance.
- Improved perception.
- Better ability to read enemy attack patterns.
- Improved dodge and parry timing assistance.
- Slight improvement to combat accuracy.


Stage 3 — Three-Tomoe Sharingan


Required card: Three-Tomoe Evolution.


Unlocks:


- Full three-tomoe Sharingan appearance.
- Stronger movement prediction.
- Improved perception of enemy attacks.
- Additional Sharingan-related combat bonuses.
- Access to eligible advanced Sharingan techniques.


Stage 4 — Mangekyou Sharingan


Required card: Mangekyou Awakening.


Requirements:


- Uchiha clan.
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan already unlocked.
- Appropriate story or progression condition.


Unlocks:


- Mangekyou Sharingan appearance.
- Advanced ocular abilities.
- Access to specific Mangekyou techniques.
- Stronger perception and combat options.


Mangekyou techniques must have meaningful chakra costs and limitations.


Stage 5 — Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan


Required card: Eternal Mangekyou Evolution.


Requirements:


- Mangekyou Sharingan already unlocked.
- Specific high-level progression requirements.


Unlocks:


- Eternal Mangekyou appearance.
- Improved mode efficiency.
- Better control of advanced ocular abilities.
- Access to further advanced techniques.


The Eternal Mangekyou must not be granted automatically when the player first obtains Sharingan.


Sharingan Card Upgrade Examples


- Sharingan Activation: unlocks Stage 1.
- Two-Tomoe Mastery: unlocks Stage 2.
- Three-Tomoe Evolution: unlocks Stage 3.
- Enhanced Perception: improves enemy attack reading.
- Chakra Perception: improves detection of chakra-based attacks.
- Mangekyou Awakening: unlocks Stage 4.
- Mangekyou Mastery: improves Mangekyou abilities.
- Eternal Mangekyou Evolution: unlocks Stage 5.
- Eternal Control: improves efficiency and reduces selected drawbacks.


These cards must have appropriate rarity and chapter requirements.


---


9. BYAKUGAN PROGRESSION


Byakugan is exclusive to the Hyuga clan.


It must also use progressive Mode Cards.


Stage 1 — Byakugan Activation


Unlocks:


- Basic Byakugan appearance.
- Improved field of vision.
- Basic chakra perception.
- Ability to detect nearby enemies.


Stage 2 — Byakugan Mastery


Unlocks:


- Improved perception range.
- Better detection of hidden enemies.
- Improved awareness of enemy positions.
- More accurate chakra-point targeting.


Stage 3 — Advanced Byakugan


Unlocks:


- Improved chakra perception.
- Better defensive awareness.
- Advanced Hyuga combat bonuses.
- Access to advanced Byakugan-related techniques.


Stage 4 — Advanced Hyuga Control


Unlocks:


- More efficient Byakugan usage.
- Improved Gentle Fist compatibility.
- Further perception improvements.
- Advanced mode enhancements.


Byakugan must not be fully upgraded from its first card.


---


10. EIGHT GATES PROGRESSION


The specialized Eight Gates system is exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not make Eight Gates available to every clan.


The player must progressively unlock the Gates through specific cards.


Gate 1 — Gate of Opening


- Initial power increase.
- Improved movement speed.
- Increased stamina consumption.


Gate 2 — Gate of Healing


- Additional combat enhancement.
- Improved physical performance.
- Higher stamina consumption.


Gate 3 — Gate of Life


- Significant speed and strength improvement.
- More demanding stamina cost.


Gate 4 — Gate of Pain


- Major damage improvement.
- Stronger physical attacks.
- More severe resource limitations.


Gate 5 — Gate of Limit


- High combat enhancement.
- Stronger movement and attack performance.


Gate 6 — Gate of View


- Advanced combat speed.
- Access to stronger techniques.
- Increased transformation limitations.


Gate 7 — Gate of Wonder


- Extremely powerful physical enhancement.
- High resource consumption.
- Strict duration limitations.


Gate 8 — Gate of Death


- Final and most powerful stage.
- Must be an exceptionally difficult progression milestone.
- Has severe consequences and a very limited duration.
- Must never be treated as an ordinary permanent stat buff.


Each Gate requires its own Mode Card or clearly defined progression card.


The player must not unlock all Eight Gates from one reward.


---


11. BIJUU PROGRESSION AND TRANSFORMATION CARDS


Bijuu are optional super-boss encounters.


The player obtains a permanent Bijuu Card only by defeating the corresponding Bijuu boss.


There are nine Bijuu:


1. Shukaku.
2. Matatabi.
3. Isobu.
4. Son Goku.
5. Kokuo.
6. Saiken.
7. Chomei.
8. Gyuki.
9. Kurama.


There are NO Bijuu Spins.


Defeating a Bijuu guarantees its permanent Bijuu Card.


However, owning the permanent Bijuu Card does NOT automatically unlock its complete transformation.


The player must progressively develop their relationship and control over that Bijuu through additional Mode Cards.


Bijuu Card — Initial Unlock


The permanent Bijuu Card:


- Confirms that the player has defeated and unlocked that Bijuu.
- Adds the Bijuu to the player's permanent collection.
- Unlocks the initial Bijuu progression tree.
- Allows the player to begin collecting its Mode Cards.
- Does NOT automatically grant the final transformation.


Bijuu Mode Card Drop Chance


After clearing a Bijuu encounter, the corresponding Bijuu Mode Card has an independent 50% chance to appear among the reward choices.


This is separate from the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card.


The 50% roll must:


- Be performed independently.
- Only apply to the corresponding Bijuu.
- Not be replaced by ordinary rarity calculations.
- Not guarantee the card every time.
- Not change the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card reward.


If the Mode Card appears, it must be included as one of the available reward choices.


If it does not appear, the player still receives the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card if this is their first defeat of that Bijuu.


Bijuu Transformation Stages


Each Bijuu has its own progression tree, but the general structure is:


Stage 1 — Bijuu Connection


- Unlocks the initial connection to the Bijuu.
- Allows limited chakra access.
- Adds a subtle chakra aura.
- Provides a small passive bonus.
- Does not unlock full transformation.


Stage 2 — Chakra Cloak


- Unlocks the first visible chakra cloak.
- Adds a more noticeable aura.
- Improves selected combat statistics.
- Grants access to a basic Bijuu-related ability.


Stage 3 — Partial Transformation


- Unlocks partial Bijuu characteristics.
- Changes selected parts of the character sprite.
- Grants stronger abilities.
- Increases chakra consumption.


Stage 4 — Advanced Partial Transformation


- Improves partial transformation control.
- Unlocks additional Bijuu abilities.
- Increases combat effectiveness.
- Requires more chakra.


Stage 5 — Advanced Bijuu Mode


- Unlocks a much stronger transformation.
- Adds a more complete visual transformation.
- Grants access to advanced Bijuu attacks.
- Requires substantial progression.


Stage 6 — Full Bijuu Transformation


- Unlocks the complete transformation, when applicable.
- Uses a dedicated transformation sprite and animation.
- Grants access to the Bijuu's most powerful abilities.
- Has significant chakra consumption and limitations.
- Requires the highest progression requirements.


Not every Bijuu needs identical attacks or identical visuals. Each must preserve its own identity, appearance, abilities, and combat style.


Example — Kurama Progression


1. Permanent Kurama Card: obtained by defeating Kurama.
2. Kurama Connection: unlocks initial chakra connection.
3. Kurama Chakra Cloak: unlocks the first cloak.
4. Kurama Chakra Control: improves control and efficiency.
5. Partial Kurama Transformation: unlocks partial transformation.
6. Advanced Kurama Control: improves advanced abilities.
7. Kurama Avatar: unlocks a stronger transformation stage.
8. Full Kurama Mode: unlocks the final available transformation stage.


Each step must be a separate progression milestone.


Do not grant Full Kurama Mode immediately after defeating Kurama.


Other Bijuu


Apply the same progression philosophy to:


- Shukaku.
- Matatabi.
- Isobu.
- Son Goku.
- Kokuo.
- Saiken.
- Chomei.
- Gyuki.


Each Bijuu must have unique:


- Mode Card names.
- Transformation artwork.
- Chakra aura.
- Sprite changes.
- Passive bonuses.
- Active abilities.
- Attack animations.
- Transformation effects.
- Progression requirements.


Do not simply recolor Kurama's transformation for the other Bijuu.


Equipping Bijuu


The player may equip only one primary Bijuu at a time.


Owning multiple permanent Bijuu Cards does not mean multiple Bijuu transformations can be active simultaneously.


The player can switch their equipped primary Bijuu outside combat through the appropriate customization or inventory interface.


---


12. RINNEGAN — SPECIAL INDEPENDENT REWARD


Rinnegan is the only independent exception to the normal clan restrictions for dojutsu.


It can be obtained regardless of the player's clan.


However:


- Rinnegan must NOT be obtainable through Dojutsu Spins.
- Rinnegan must NOT be an ordinary card in the normal reward pool.
- Rinnegan has an independent 0.5% chance to appear as an additional reward choice after clearing an eligible room.
- The 0.5% chance is a separate roll and must not replace ordinary card choices.
- It must become a permanent unlock when obtained.
- It must have its own progression and upgrade cards.
- Its advanced abilities must still require appropriate progression.


The Rinnegan must be extremely rare and should feel like a special discovery.


Do not confuse this 0.5% independent reward chance with the Mythical card rarity probability.


They are two separate systems.


---


13. CARD COMPATIBILITY AND CLAN RESTRICTIONS


Cards must respect the character's clan, lineage, element, bloodline, and unlocked modes.


Examples:


- Sharingan cards: Uchiha only.
- Mangekyou cards: Uchiha with the required previous Sharingan stages.
- Eternal Mangekyou cards: Uchiha with Mangekyou already unlocked.
- Byakugan cards: Hyuga only.
- Eight Gates cards: Lee/Guy lineage only.
- Specialized Hyuga techniques: Hyuga only.
- Specialized Uchiha techniques: Uchiha only.
- Bijuu Mode Cards: require the corresponding permanent Bijuu Card.
- Rinnegan: independent exception, with its own unlock conditions.


The reward generator must check compatibility before displaying a card.


Never offer a player an exclusive card they cannot use.


If a card requires another card, show that requirement clearly.


---


14. MODE ACTIVATION AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT


Modes must be activated through a dedicated mode control.


The player must be able to:


- Activate an unlocked mode.
- Deactivate it.
- See its current stage.
- See its chakra or stamina consumption.
- See its duration or limitations.
- Understand which abilities are available while it is active.


Different modes must have different resource demands.


Examples:


- Sharingan: moderate chakra drain.
- Mangekyou: higher chakra drain.
- Eternal Mangekyou: improved efficiency compared to Mangekyou, but still requires chakra.
- Byakugan: moderate chakra drain.
- Bijuu transformations: substantial chakra drain depending on stage.
- Eight Gates: significant stamina and other progression-specific limitations.


Do not allow every mode to remain active indefinitely without resource costs.


Mode cards may improve:


- Chakra efficiency.
- Transformation duration.
- Damage.
- Defense.
- Movement.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Transformation control.
- Specific mode abilities.


Every improvement must be clearly described and balanced.


---


15. CARD UPGRADE LEVELS


Cards that support upgrades must have defined levels.


Example:


Fireball Jutsu


- Level 1: Basic Fireball.
- Level 2: Increased damage.
- Level 3: Larger projectile.
- Level 4: Improved range and impact.
- Level 5: Advanced Fireball version.


Chakra Reserve


- Level 1: +10 maximum chakra.
- Level 2: +20 maximum chakra.
- Level 3: +30 maximum chakra.
- Level 4: +40 maximum chakra.
- Level 5: +50 maximum chakra.


Parry Mastery


- Level 1: Small parry reward improvement.
- Level 2: Increased stamina recovery.
- Level 3: Improved counterattack damage.
- Level 4: Improved chakra recovery.
- Level 5: Advanced defensive bonus.


These are examples of how card levels should work. Each card must have its own balanced upgrade path.


Mode Cards must use stage-based progression where appropriate, not simply repeat the same numerical bonus.


For example, a Sharingan evolution card unlocks a new stage rather than merely adding +5% damage.


---


16. CARD INTERFACE AND REWARD PRESENTATION


The card reward screen must be visually clear and fully usable in landscape orientation.


Display:


- Card artwork.
- Card name.
- Rarity frame.
- Short description.
- Main effect.
- Important numerical values.
- Permanent or temporary indicator.
- Compatibility requirements.
- Upgrade level or next stage.


When a player selects a card:


1. Show a selection animation.
2. Display the card's full effect.
3. Confirm the selection.
4. Apply the effect correctly.
5. Update the player's collection or current run.
6. Return to the next room or progression screen.


The player must never receive a card without knowing what it does.


Do not use placeholder text such as "Increases power" without defining the actual effect.


---


17. REQUIRED CARD DATABASE


Create a structured card database containing every card in the game.


Each card entry must include:


- Unique card ID.
- Card name.
- Category.
- Rarity.
- Description.
- Effect.
- Numerical values.
- Permanent or temporary status.
- Minimum chapter.
- Unlock requirements.
- Clan compatibility.
- Element compatibility.
- Mode compatibility.
- Upgrade path.
- Maximum level or stage.
- Acquisition source.
- Whether it can appear in ordinary room rewards.
- Whether it is a special boss drop.
- Whether it is part of a Bijuu progression tree.


Do not generate cards with missing information.


Do not use one generic effect for dozens of different cards.


Every card must have a specific gameplay purpose.


---


18. FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES


1. Cards are the central system for acquiring skills, buffs, weapons, modes, and upgrades.
2. Standard rooms generate exactly 4 card choices.
3. Elite rooms generate 5 choices.
4. Mini-boss rooms generate 6 choices.
5. Main boss rooms generate 7 choices.
6. Optional Bijuu encounters generate 8 choices.
7. Card rarity probabilities must follow the defined progression tables.
8. Card eligibility must respect chapter progression and unlock requirements.
9. Exclusive clan abilities must never be offered to incompatible clans.
10. Sharingan and its evolutions are exclusive to Uchiha.
11. Byakugan is exclusive to Hyuga.
12. Eight Gates and specialized Lee/Guy taijutsu are exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
13. Rinnegan is the only independent dojutsu exception and has a separate 0.5% eligible-room reward roll.
14. Rinnegan is not available through Dojutsu Spins.
15. Bijuu are obtained by defeating their individual optional super-bosses, never through spins.
16. Defeating a Bijuu guarantees its permanent Bijuu Card.
17. The corresponding Bijuu Mode Card has a separate 50% chance to appear among the reward choices after the encounter.
18. Owning a permanent Bijuu Card does not automatically unlock its complete transformation.
19. Sharingan, Byakugan, Eight Gates, and Bijuu modes must be progressively evolved through their respective cards.
20. Special boss drops and independent special rewards must not replace ordinary card reward choices.
21. Every card must have a defined effect, rarity, eligibility, and acquisition method.
22. Do not leave card effects, probabilities, progression requirements, or mode stages undefined.
23. Do not replace this system with generic level-up rewards or automatic full unlocks.


The goal is to create a deep progression system where every card choice matters, every transformation feels earned, and players gradually build their own combat style through meaningful rewards.

PART 5 — COMPLETE CARD SYSTEM, CARD RARITY, DROP RATES, PROGRESSION AND MODE EVOLUTION

1. CORE CARD SYSTEM — NON-NEGOTIABLE RULE


Cards are the central progression and build-customization system of the entire game.


The player must obtain skills, passive abilities, stat upgrades, weapons, transformations, mode evolutions, and special enhancements through cards.


Do NOT create a separate generic skill-unlock system that bypasses cards.


Do NOT automatically grant fully upgraded abilities or transformations when the player first unlocks them.


Every card must have a clearly defined purpose, rarity, effect, compatibility requirement, progression stage, and acquisition method.


There are two main types of card progression:


1. Permanent Cards: Permanently unlock a skill, ability, weapon, mode, or progression upgrade. Once obtained, they remain in the player's collection.
2. Run Cards: Provide temporary bonuses during the current run. They are lost when the run ends or the player dies, unless a specific permanent effect says otherwise.


Some permanent abilities require multiple additional cards to reach their full potential. Unlocking the base ability does NOT automatically unlock every upgrade.


---


2. CARD CATEGORIES


Organize the card collection into the following categories:


A. Active Skill Cards


Unlock abilities that the player can actively use during combat.


Examples:


- Fireball Jutsu
- Chidori
- Rasengan
- Shadow Clone Jutsu
- Substitution Technique
- Gentle Fist
- Rotation
- Lightning-based attacks
- Weapon techniques
- Clan-exclusive abilities


Each active skill card must define:


- Skill name
- Skill description
- Card rarity
- Chakra cost
- Cooldown
- Damage
- Range
- Area of effect
- Startup time
- Recovery time
- Upgrade possibilities
- Clan, element, bloodline, or mode requirements
- Whether the skill is permanent or temporary


B. Passive Ability Cards


Provide permanent or temporary passive effects.


Examples:


- Increased maximum health
- Increased maximum chakra
- Increased stamina
- Faster chakra regeneration
- Increased critical-hit chance
- Increased critical-hit damage
- Reduced cooldowns
- Increased movement speed
- Increased weapon damage
- Increased resistance to specific elements
- Improved healing effects
- Improved parry recovery


Passive cards must have balanced values and clear descriptions.


C. Stat Upgrade Cards


Directly improve player statistics.


Examples:


- Vitality: +10 maximum health.
- Chakra Reserve: +10 maximum chakra.
- Stamina Training: +10 maximum stamina.
- Focus: +5% skill damage.
- Weapon Mastery: +5% weapon damage.
- Quick Recovery: +5% cooldown recovery speed.


These cards may have multiple upgrade levels.


Do not allow unlimited stacking of the same bonus without a defined maximum.


D. Weapon Cards


Unlock weapons or weapon-related improvements.


Examples:


- Kunai Mastery
- Katana Mastery
- Dual Blade Mastery
- Heavy Sword Mastery
- Chakra Blade Mastery
- Staff Mastery
- Shuriken Mastery
- Special Boss Weapons


Some weapons must be obtained through specific boss drops rather than ordinary random card rewards.


E. Mode Cards


These cards progressively unlock and improve special modes.


Examples:


- Sharingan Activation
- Sharingan Mastery
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan
- Mangekyou Sharingan
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan
- Byakugan Mastery
- Eight Gates progression
- Bijuu Chakra Control
- Bijuu Transformation Stages
- Kurama Chakra Control


Mode Cards are especially important and must follow the progressive evolution system described later in this document.


F. Run Enhancement Cards


These cards provide temporary effects for the current run.


Examples:


- +20% damage for the current run.
- +15% maximum health for the current run.
- +10% movement speed for the current run.
- +20% chakra regeneration for the current run.
- +10% critical-hit chance for the current run.
- Reduced cooldowns for the current run.


Run Enhancement Cards must be clearly marked as temporary.


---


3. CARD RARITY SYSTEM


Every card has one of six rarities.


Use these exact base rarity probabilities for the rarity roll:


Rarity| Base Probability
Common| 50%
Uncommon| 25%
Rare| 15%
Epic| 7%
Legendary| 2.5%
Mythical| 0.5%


These probabilities represent the base rarity distribution, not the chance of receiving a specific named card.


The game must perform the rarity roll first, then select an eligible card from that rarity's pool.


A card's rarity determines its potential power, complexity, and uniqueness, but rarity alone must not make a card useless or automatically superior in every situation.


COMMON


- Basic and accessible effects.
- Small stat improvements.
- Basic combat skills.
- Early progression cards.
- Simple weapon improvements.


Examples:


- +5 maximum health.
- +5 maximum chakra.
- Basic Kunai Mastery.
- Small movement-speed increase.
- Basic Fireball improvement.


UNCOMMON


- Improved versions of basic abilities.
- Moderate stat improvements.
- Basic combinations of effects.
- Additional utility.


Examples:


- +10 maximum health.
- +5% weapon damage.
- Improved Fireball damage.
- Faster stamina recovery.
- Improved basic combo damage.


RARE


- Strong combat improvements.
- More specialized abilities.
- Meaningful upgrades to existing skills.
- More powerful passive effects.


Examples:


- Chidori enhancement.
- Improved Shadow Clone Jutsu.
- Increased critical-hit chance.
- Improved dash recovery.
- Sharingan perception enhancement.


EPIC


- Powerful abilities and advanced upgrades.
- Special combat mechanics.
- Major improvements to existing modes.
- Strong combinations of effects.


Examples:


- Advanced Chidori.
- Mangekyou progression card.
- Advanced Byakugan perception.
- Eight Gates advancement.
- Powerful weapon techniques.


LEGENDARY


- Extremely powerful and specialized cards.
- Unique abilities.
- Major transformation improvements.
- Rare boss-related abilities.
- High-impact permanent upgrades.


Examples:


- Susanoo progression card.
- Advanced Bijuu Chakra Control.
- Eight Gates higher-stage progression.
- Powerful signature boss techniques.
- Advanced transformation mastery.


MYTHICAL


- Extremely rare, exceptional cards.
- Unique or highly specialized effects.
- Major milestones in progression.
- Special abilities that significantly change a build.


Examples:


- Eternal Mangekyou progression.
- Advanced Bijuu transformation evolution.
- Extremely rare unique techniques.
- Special high-level mode enhancements.


Mythical cards must remain exceptionally rare. Do not fill the ordinary card pool with mythical cards just to make rewards feel more exciting.


---


4. CARD DROP PROBABILITIES AND REWARD RULES


Every room must follow the established reward-choice system.


Standard Room


After clearing a standard room:


- Generate exactly 4 card choices.
- The player selects exactly 1 card.
- The other choices disappear.
- The selected card is added to the player's collection or current run, depending on its type.


Elite and Difficult Rooms


Harder rooms must provide additional choices and better reward quality.


Use this progression:


- Standard Room: 4 choices.
- Elite Room: 5 choices.
- Mini-Boss Room: 6 choices.
- Main Boss Room: 7 choices.
- Optional Bijuu Challenge: 8 choices.


Higher difficulty should improve the reward quality and may increase the probability of higher rarities, without making powerful cards guaranteed.


Rarity Scaling by Progression


The rarity probabilities must evolve as the player advances through the story.


Use the following base progression:


Early Game — Chapter 1


- Common: 65%
- Uncommon: 25%
- Rare: 8%
- Epic: 1.8%
- Legendary: 0.19%
- Mythical: 0.01%


Early-Mid Game — Chapters 2–3


- Common: 55%
- Uncommon: 27%
- Rare: 13%
- Epic: 4%
- Legendary: 0.9%
- Mythical: 0.1%


Mid Game — Chapters 4–5


- Common: 45%
- Uncommon: 28%
- Rare: 17%
- Epic: 7%
- Legendary: 2.5%
- Mythical: 0.5%


Late Game — Chapters 6–7


- Common: 35%
- Uncommon: 28%
- Rare: 20%
- Epic: 10%
- Legendary: 5.5%
- Mythical: 1.5%


Final Chapter — Chapter 8


- Common: 30%
- Uncommon: 25%
- Rare: 22%
- Epic: 13%
- Legendary: 7.5%
- Mythical: 2.5%


Each progression table totals 100%.


These probabilities determine the rarity of each generated card choice. The game must still generate the correct number of choices for the room.


The card pool must also be restricted by progression. A player in Chapter 1 must not receive endgame abilities simply because a high rarity was rolled.


A Legendary card can only appear when its specific progression requirements are met.


A Mythical card can only appear when its specific progression requirements are met.


The game must use both:


1. Rarity probability.
2. Card eligibility based on chapter, unlocks, character compatibility, and progression.


A high rarity roll does not override eligibility restrictions.


Important Reward Separation


Special rewards must not silently replace ordinary card choices.


The following systems are independent:


- Ordinary card reward generation.
- Specific boss signature drops.
- Guaranteed permanent Bijuu card rewards.
- The 50% Bijuu Mode Card appearance chance.
- The independent 0.5% Rinnegan reward chance.


Each system must be processed separately and clearly.


---


5. WHEN EACH CARD CAN FIRST APPEAR


Every card must have a minimum chapter or unlock requirement.


Use these general progression rules:


Chapter 1 — Basic Foundation


Available cards:


- Basic weapon cards.
- Basic combat abilities.
- Basic elemental abilities.
- Basic health, chakra, and stamina upgrades.
- Basic movement and defense upgrades.
- Common and Uncommon cards.
- A limited selection of Rare cards.


Do not allow advanced transformations or endgame abilities to appear.


Chapters 2–3 — Intermediate Abilities


Introduce:


- More advanced elemental jutsu.
- Clan-specific abilities.
- Weapon specialization.
- Improved combat passives.
- Basic bloodline abilities.
- Early stages of eligible dojutsu progression.
- More Rare and Epic cards.


Chapters 4–5 — Advanced Combat


Introduce:


- Advanced clan abilities.
- Stronger elemental techniques.
- Advanced bloodline abilities.
- More powerful dojutsu progression cards.
- Advanced weapon techniques.
- Early high-level transformation improvements.
- Legendary cards with appropriate unlock requirements.


Chapters 6–7 — High-Level Progression


Introduce:


- Advanced dojutsu upgrades.
- Powerful clan techniques.
- Advanced transformations.
- High-level Bijuu progression cards, if the player already owns the corresponding Bijuu.
- Rare signature boss techniques.
- More Legendary and Mythical cards.


Chapter 8 — Endgame


Introduce:


- Final-stage progression cards.
- Highest-level transformation improvements.
- Extremely powerful special abilities.
- Endgame passive upgrades.
- Mythical cards with strict requirements.


These are minimum progression guidelines. Individual cards must have their own specific unlock conditions.


A card must never appear if the player cannot use it and has no valid path to unlock it.


---


6. DUPLICATE CARDS AND CARD COLLECTION


When the player receives a card they already own:


- If it is a permanent card with upgrade levels, allow the duplicate to contribute toward its next upgrade when applicable.
- If the card is already at maximum level, convert it into Duplicate Compensation.
- If it is a temporary Run Card, handle duplicates according to its stacking rules.
- Never silently delete a duplicate without giving the player a defined result.


The collection interface must display:


- Card name.
- Card artwork.
- Rarity.
- Current level.
- Maximum level.
- Effect.
- Upgrade requirements.
- Acquisition source.
- Compatibility requirements.
- Whether the card is permanent or temporary.


The player must be able to inspect locked cards and see their unlock conditions.


---


7. PROGRESSIVE MODE EVOLUTION — EXTREMELY IMPORTANT


Special modes must NOT be fully unlocked when the player obtains their first related card.


The player must progressively develop each mode by collecting specific Mode Cards.


The first card should unlock the initial functionality, not the complete transformation.


Additional cards unlock new stages, improve control, increase effectiveness, and grant new abilities.


This applies to:


- Sharingan.
- Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.
- Byakugan.
- Eight Gates.
- Bijuu modes.
- Other advanced transformations.


Each mode must have a progression tree with clear stages and requirements.


The player must be able to see:


- Current mode stage.
- Next available stage.
- Required cards.
- Current bonuses.
- New abilities unlocked by each stage.
- Chakra or stamina costs.
- Transformation duration or limitations.
- Visual appearance of each stage.


Do not automatically unlock all stages after obtaining the first card.


---


8. SHARINGAN PROGRESSION


Sharingan is exclusive to the Uchiha clan.


A non-Uchiha character must never obtain Sharingan through ordinary cards, spins, or random rewards.


The player must progressively evolve the Sharingan through Mode Cards.


Stage 1 — Sharingan Activation


Required card: Sharingan Activation.


Unlocks:


- Basic Sharingan activation.
- Red eye appearance with one tomoe.
- Slightly improved enemy movement perception.
- Small reaction-time improvement.
- Basic chakra perception.


This is only the initial Sharingan stage.


Stage 2 — Two-Tomoe Sharingan


Required card: Two-Tomoe Mastery.


Unlocks:


- Two-tomoe appearance.
- Improved perception.
- Better ability to read enemy attack patterns.
- Improved dodge and parry timing assistance.
- Slight improvement to combat accuracy.


Stage 3 — Three-Tomoe Sharingan


Required card: Three-Tomoe Evolution.


Unlocks:


- Full three-tomoe Sharingan appearance.
- Stronger movement prediction.
- Improved perception of enemy attacks.
- Additional Sharingan-related combat bonuses.
- Access to eligible advanced Sharingan techniques.


Stage 4 — Mangekyou Sharingan


Required card: Mangekyou Awakening.


Requirements:


- Uchiha clan.
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan already unlocked.
- Appropriate story or progression condition.


Unlocks:


- Mangekyou Sharingan appearance.
- Advanced ocular abilities.
- Access to specific Mangekyou techniques.
- Stronger perception and combat options.


Mangekyou techniques must have meaningful chakra costs and limitations.


Stage 5 — Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan


Required card: Eternal Mangekyou Evolution.


Requirements:


- Mangekyou Sharingan already unlocked.
- Specific high-level progression requirements.


Unlocks:


- Eternal Mangekyou appearance.
- Improved mode efficiency.
- Better control of advanced ocular abilities.
- Access to further advanced techniques.


The Eternal Mangekyou must not be granted automatically when the player first obtains Sharingan.


Sharingan Card Upgrade Examples


- Sharingan Activation: unlocks Stage 1.
- Two-Tomoe Mastery: unlocks Stage 2.
- Three-Tomoe Evolution: unlocks Stage 3.
- Enhanced Perception: improves enemy attack reading.
- Chakra Perception: improves detection of chakra-based attacks.
- Mangekyou Awakening: unlocks Stage 4.
- Mangekyou Mastery: improves Mangekyou abilities.
- Eternal Mangekyou Evolution: unlocks Stage 5.
- Eternal Control: improves efficiency and reduces selected drawbacks.


These cards must have appropriate rarity and chapter requirements.


---


9. BYAKUGAN PROGRESSION


Byakugan is exclusive to the Hyuga clan.


It must also use progressive Mode Cards.


Stage 1 — Byakugan Activation


Unlocks:


- Basic Byakugan appearance.
- Improved field of vision.
- Basic chakra perception.
- Ability to detect nearby enemies.


Stage 2 — Byakugan Mastery


Unlocks:


- Improved perception range.
- Better detection of hidden enemies.
- Improved awareness of enemy positions.
- More accurate chakra-point targeting.


Stage 3 — Advanced Byakugan


Unlocks:


- Improved chakra perception.
- Better defensive awareness.
- Advanced Hyuga combat bonuses.
- Access to advanced Byakugan-related techniques.


Stage 4 — Advanced Hyuga Control


Unlocks:


- More efficient Byakugan usage.
- Improved Gentle Fist compatibility.
- Further perception improvements.
- Advanced mode enhancements.


Byakugan must not be fully upgraded from its first card.


---


10. EIGHT GATES PROGRESSION


The specialized Eight Gates system is exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not make Eight Gates available to every clan.


The player must progressively unlock the Gates through specific cards.


Gate 1 — Gate of Opening


- Initial power increase.
- Improved movement speed.
- Increased stamina consumption.


Gate 2 — Gate of Healing


- Additional combat enhancement.
- Improved physical performance.
- Higher stamina consumption.


Gate 3 — Gate of Life


- Significant speed and strength improvement.
- More demanding stamina cost.


Gate 4 — Gate of Pain


- Major damage improvement.
- Stronger physical attacks.
- More severe resource limitations.


Gate 5 — Gate of Limit


- High combat enhancement.
- Stronger movement and attack performance.


Gate 6 — Gate of View


- Advanced combat speed.
- Access to stronger techniques.
- Increased transformation limitations.


Gate 7 — Gate of Wonder


- Extremely powerful physical enhancement.
- High resource consumption.
- Strict duration limitations.


Gate 8 — Gate of Death


- Final and most powerful stage.
- Must be an exceptionally difficult progression milestone.
- Has severe consequences and a very limited duration.
- Must never be treated as an ordinary permanent stat buff.


Each Gate requires its own Mode Card or clearly defined progression card.


The player must not unlock all Eight Gates from one reward.


---


11. BIJUU PROGRESSION AND TRANSFORMATION CARDS


Bijuu are optional super-boss encounters.


The player obtains a permanent Bijuu Card only by defeating the corresponding Bijuu boss.


There are nine Bijuu:


1. Shukaku.
2. Matatabi.
3. Isobu.
4. Son Goku.
5. Kokuo.
6. Saiken.
7. Chomei.
8. Gyuki.
9. Kurama.


There are NO Bijuu Spins.


Defeating a Bijuu guarantees its permanent Bijuu Card.


However, owning the permanent Bijuu Card does NOT automatically unlock its complete transformation.


The player must progressively develop their relationship and control over that Bijuu through additional Mode Cards.


Bijuu Card — Initial Unlock


The permanent Bijuu Card:


- Confirms that the player has defeated and unlocked that Bijuu.
- Adds the Bijuu to the player's permanent collection.
- Unlocks the initial Bijuu progression tree.
- Allows the player to begin collecting its Mode Cards.
- Does NOT automatically grant the final transformation.


Bijuu Mode Card Drop Chance


After clearing a Bijuu encounter, the corresponding Bijuu Mode Card has an independent 50% chance to appear among the reward choices.


This is separate from the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card.


The 50% roll must:


- Be performed independently.
- Only apply to the corresponding Bijuu.
- Not be replaced by ordinary rarity calculations.
- Not guarantee the card every time.
- Not change the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card reward.


If the Mode Card appears, it must be included as one of the available reward choices.


If it does not appear, the player still receives the guaranteed permanent Bijuu Card if this is their first defeat of that Bijuu.


Bijuu Transformation Stages


Each Bijuu has its own progression tree, but the general structure is:


Stage 1 — Bijuu Connection


- Unlocks the initial connection to the Bijuu.
- Allows limited chakra access.
- Adds a subtle chakra aura.
- Provides a small passive bonus.
- Does not unlock full transformation.


Stage 2 — Chakra Cloak


- Unlocks the first visible chakra cloak.
- Adds a more noticeable aura.
- Improves selected combat statistics.
- Grants access to a basic Bijuu-related ability.


Stage 3 — Partial Transformation


- Unlocks partial Bijuu characteristics.
- Changes selected parts of the character sprite.
- Grants stronger abilities.
- Increases chakra consumption.


Stage 4 — Advanced Partial Transformation


- Improves partial transformation control.
- Unlocks additional Bijuu abilities.
- Increases combat effectiveness.
- Requires more chakra.


Stage 5 — Advanced Bijuu Mode


- Unlocks a much stronger transformation.
- Adds a more complete visual transformation.
- Grants access to advanced Bijuu attacks.
- Requires substantial progression.


Stage 6 — Full Bijuu Transformation


- Unlocks the complete transformation, when applicable.
- Uses a dedicated transformation sprite and animation.
- Grants access to the Bijuu's most powerful abilities.
- Has significant chakra consumption and limitations.
- Requires the highest progression requirements.


Not every Bijuu needs identical attacks or identical visuals. Each must preserve its own identity, appearance, abilities, and combat style.


Example — Kurama Progression


1. Permanent Kurama Card: obtained by defeating Kurama.
2. Kurama Connection: unlocks initial chakra connection.
3. Kurama Chakra Cloak: unlocks the first cloak.
4. Kurama Chakra Control: improves control and efficiency.
5. Partial Kurama Transformation: unlocks partial transformation.
6. Advanced Kurama Control: improves advanced abilities.
7. Kurama Avatar: unlocks a stronger transformation stage.
8. Full Kurama Mode: unlocks the final available transformation stage.


Each step must be a separate progression milestone.


Do not grant Full Kurama Mode immediately after defeating Kurama.


Other Bijuu


Apply the same progression philosophy to:


- Shukaku.
- Matatabi.
- Isobu.
- Son Goku.
- Kokuo.
- Saiken.
- Chomei.
- Gyuki.


Each Bijuu must have unique:


- Mode Card names.
- Transformation artwork.
- Chakra aura.
- Sprite changes.
- Passive bonuses.
- Active abilities.
- Attack animations.
- Transformation effects.
- Progression requirements.


Do not simply recolor Kurama's transformation for the other Bijuu.


Equipping Bijuu


The player may equip only one primary Bijuu at a time.


Owning multiple permanent Bijuu Cards does not mean multiple Bijuu transformations can be active simultaneously.


The player can switch their equipped primary Bijuu outside combat through the appropriate customization or inventory interface.


---


12. RINNEGAN — SPECIAL INDEPENDENT REWARD


Rinnegan is the only independent exception to the normal clan restrictions for dojutsu.


It can be obtained regardless of the player's clan.


However:


- Rinnegan must NOT be obtainable through Dojutsu Spins.
- Rinnegan must NOT be an ordinary card in the normal reward pool.
- Rinnegan has an independent 0.5% chance to appear as an additional reward choice after clearing an eligible room.
- The 0.5% chance is a separate roll and must not replace ordinary card choices.
- It must become a permanent unlock when obtained.
- It must have its own progression and upgrade cards.
- Its advanced abilities must still require appropriate progression.


The Rinnegan must be extremely rare and should feel like a special discovery.


Do not confuse this 0.5% independent reward chance with the Mythical card rarity probability.


They are two separate systems.


---


13. CARD COMPATIBILITY AND CLAN RESTRICTIONS


Cards must respect the character's clan, lineage, element, bloodline, and unlocked modes.


Examples:


- Sharingan cards: Uchiha only.
- Mangekyou cards: Uchiha with the required previous Sharingan stages.
- Eternal Mangekyou cards: Uchiha with Mangekyou already unlocked.
- Byakugan cards: Hyuga only.
- Eight Gates cards: Lee/Guy lineage only.
- Specialized Hyuga techniques: Hyuga only.
- Specialized Uchiha techniques: Uchiha only.
- Bijuu Mode Cards: require the corresponding permanent Bijuu Card.
- Rinnegan: independent exception, with its own unlock conditions.


The reward generator must check compatibility before displaying a card.


Never offer a player an exclusive card they cannot use.


If a card requires another card, show that requirement clearly.


---


14. MODE ACTIVATION AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT


Modes must be activated through a dedicated mode control.


The player must be able to:


- Activate an unlocked mode.
- Deactivate it.
- See its current stage.
- See its chakra or stamina consumption.
- See its duration or limitations.
- Understand which abilities are available while it is active.


Different modes must have different resource demands.


Examples:


- Sharingan: moderate chakra drain.
- Mangekyou: higher chakra drain.
- Eternal Mangekyou: improved efficiency compared to Mangekyou, but still requires chakra.
- Byakugan: moderate chakra drain.
- Bijuu transformations: substantial chakra drain depending on stage.
- Eight Gates: significant stamina and other progression-specific limitations.


Do not allow every mode to remain active indefinitely without resource costs.


Mode cards may improve:


- Chakra efficiency.
- Transformation duration.
- Damage.
- Defense.
- Movement.
- Ability cooldowns.
- Transformation control.
- Specific mode abilities.


Every improvement must be clearly described and balanced.


---


15. CARD UPGRADE LEVELS


Cards that support upgrades must have defined levels.


Example:


Fireball Jutsu


- Level 1: Basic Fireball.
- Level 2: Increased damage.
- Level 3: Larger projectile.
- Level 4: Improved range and impact.
- Level 5: Advanced Fireball version.


Chakra Reserve


- Level 1: +10 maximum chakra.
- Level 2: +20 maximum chakra.
- Level 3: +30 maximum chakra.
- Level 4: +40 maximum chakra.
- Level 5: +50 maximum chakra.


Parry Mastery


- Level 1: Small parry reward improvement.
- Level 2: Increased stamina recovery.
- Level 3: Improved counterattack damage.
- Level 4: Improved chakra recovery.
- Level 5: Advanced defensive bonus.


These are examples of how card levels should work. Each card must have its own balanced upgrade path.


Mode Cards must use stage-based progression where appropriate, not simply repeat the same numerical bonus.


For example, a Sharingan evolution card unlocks a new stage rather than merely adding +5% damage.


---


16. CARD INTERFACE AND REWARD PRESENTATION


The card reward screen must be visually clear and fully usable in landscape orientation.


Display:


- Card artwork.
- Card name.
- Rarity frame.
- Short description.
- Main effect.
- Important numerical values.
- Permanent or temporary indicator.
- Compatibility requirements.
- Upgrade level or next stage.


When a player selects a card:


1. Show a selection animation.
2. Display the card's full effect.
3. Confirm the selection.
4. Apply the effect correctly.
5. Update the player's collection or current run.
6. Return to the next room or progression screen.


The player must never receive a card without knowing what it does.


Do not use placeholder text such as "Increases power" without defining the actual effect.


---


17. REQUIRED CARD DATABASE


Create a structured card database containing every card in the game.


Each card entry must include:


- Unique card ID.
- Card name.
- Category.
- Rarity.
- Description.
- Effect.
- Numerical values.
- Permanent or temporary status.
- Minimum chapter.
- Unlock requirements.
- Clan compatibility.
- Element compatibility.
- Mode compatibility.
- Upgrade path.
- Maximum level or stage.
- Acquisition source.
- Whether it can appear in ordinary room rewards.
- Whether it is a special boss drop.
- Whether it is part of a Bijuu progression tree.


Do not generate cards with missing information.


Do not use one generic effect for dozens of different cards.


Every card must have a specific gameplay purpose.


---


18. FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES


1. Cards are the central system for acquiring skills, buffs, weapons, modes, and upgrades.
2. Standard rooms generate exactly 4 card choices.
3. Elite rooms generate 5 choices.
4. Mini-boss rooms generate 6 choices.
5. Main boss rooms generate 7 choices.
6. Optional Bijuu encounters generate 8 choices.
7. Card rarity probabilities must follow the defined progression tables.
8. Card eligibility must respect chapter progression and unlock requirements.
9. Exclusive clan abilities must never be offered to incompatible clans.
10. Sharingan and its evolutions are exclusive to Uchiha.
11. Byakugan is exclusive to Hyuga.
12. Eight Gates and specialized Lee/Guy taijutsu are exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
13. Rinnegan is the only independent dojutsu exception and has a separate 0.5% eligible-room reward roll.
14. Rinnegan is not available through Dojutsu Spins.
15. Bijuu are obtained by defeating their individual optional super-bosses, never through spins.
16. Defeating a Bijuu guarantees its permanent Bijuu Card.
17. The corresponding Bijuu Mode Card has a separate 50% chance to appear among the reward choices after the encounter.
18. Owning a permanent Bijuu Card does not automatically unlock its complete transformation.
19. Sharingan, Byakugan, Eight Gates, and Bijuu modes must be progressively evolved through their respective cards.
20. Special boss drops and independent special rewards must not replace ordinary card reward choices.
21. Every card must have a defined effect, rarity, eligibility, and acquisition method.
22. Do not leave card effects, probabilities, progression requirements, or mode stages undefined.
23. Do not replace this system with generic level-up rewards or automatic full unlocks.


The goal is to create a deep progression system where every card choice matters, every transformation feels earned, and players gradually build their own combat style through meaningful rewards.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete a polished, playable HTML/Canvas 2D Naruto-inspired action roguelike with story progression, permanent progression, run rewards, inventory, customization, audio/settings, collection interfaces, and additional modes.

## Requirements
- Preserve `960 × 540` logical resolution, 16:9 shell, mobile controls, fixed-step combat, `ashesSave` persistence, and `480 × 270` internal rendering intent.
- Keep permanent progression separate from temporary run cards and upgrades.
- Preserve exact 3/4/5/6/7/8-card horizontal rewards, one selection per eligible room, independent 0.5% Rinnegan rewards, Bijuu unlocks, exact 50% Bijuu Mode Card rolls, and normal story rooms using 4 choices.
- Preserve clan, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Lee/Guy gate, weapon, and lineage restrictions.
- Preserve 2D side-view gameplay, landscape-only layouts, and the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture.
- Implement inventory, equipment, weapon switching, customization, settings/audio, hub NPC logic, achievements, collections, and additional modes without speculative systems.

## Decisions
- Permanent progression and temporary run builds remain separate.
- Rinnegan stays independent from ordinary rewards and permanent spin pools.
- Bijuu permanent unlocks remain separate from temporary card rolls.
- The compact Chapter 1–8 routing framework remains the implementation bridge until exact Part 3 room graphs are available.
- Story rooms use exact-count reward selection rather than legacy wave/reward flow.
- `RUN_CARD_DB` represents the temporary run-card pool; `storyRewardOptions(count)` returns exactly `count` distinct cards when sufficient cards exist.
- The enemy-clear branch must call `completeStoryRoom()` for every story room.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented title shell, 16:9 presentation, HUD, progression modal, controls, portrait handling, mobile touch controls, and settings-oriented UI structure.
- Implemented fixed-step movement, combat, AI, projectiles, particles, resources, saves, defeat/victory, and fixed-step update behavior.
- Implemented clans, permanent spin pools, rarity rolls, duplicate shards, bloodline and ocular restrictions, Sharingan, Byakugan, elements, Lee/Guy gates, weapons, and lineage progression.
- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, Bijuu challenges, permanent Bijuu equipment, and primary Bijuu behavior.
- Implemented permanent identity saves and temporary-run reset behavior.
- Added deterministic Chapter 1–8 routing, room indexing, story reward generation, compact story-room routing, and chapter-map hooks.
- Added `STORY_CHAPTERS`, `storyRewardOptions`, `applyRunReward`, `startStoryRoom`, `showChapterMap`, `completeStoryRoom`, and `finishRoomChoice`.
- Replaced the legacy reward option pool with the structured, distinct-card `RUN_CARD_DB` presentation layer.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.
- Identified the remaining legacy enemy-clear branch still calling `showRewards()` instead of `completeStoryRoom()`.

### Active
- Replace legacy wave/reward clearing completely with `completeStoryRoom()` for every story room.
- Enforce exactly one reward selection per eligible room and retain Rinnegan reveal handling outside ordinary rewards.
- Integrate story clearing with existing enemy-clear and update logic.
- Replace `showRewards()` with exact-count `storyRewardOptions()` presentation.
- Complete inventory, permanent/temporary equipment separation, customization, settings/audio, hub, achievements, and collection interfaces.
- Implement additional modes and presentation/combat polish.

### Blocked
- Exact full Part 3 room graphs and boss/drop tables remain unavailable.
- Desktop and mobile landscape gameplay verification remains incomplete.
- Exact boss phases, signature drops, dedicated Bijuu cutscenes, and 77+ room details cannot be finalized without exact specifications.

## Next Move
1. Patch the enemy-clear branch in `update()` to call `completeStoryRoom()` and avoid the legacy wave/reward branch.
2. Replace `showRewards()` with exact-count `storyRewardOptions()` cards and enforce one selection with a continue gate.
3. Keep Rinnegan reveal handling independent from ordinary cards.
4. Complete inventory, permanent/temporary equipment separation, weapon switching, customization, settings/audio, hub, achievements, and collection interfaces.
5. Implement additional modes and presentation/combat polish.
6. Add exact routing, reconnections, environments, hazards, merchants, healing, treasure, challenges, and secrets once specifications are available.
7. Run `node --check game.js`, launch the game, and verify desktop and mobile landscape layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Main combat, routing, cards, inventory, progression, bosses, modes, and saves.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Canvas shell, title, HUD, modal, and mobile controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css`: 16:9 shell, reward/card presentation, responsive layout, and mobile styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: Local launch entry point.

## Important Context
- Existing project files are uncommitted and untracked.
- Normal story-cleared rooms require 4 choices; difficult rooms and bosses use 3/5/6/7/8 choices according to final room definitions.
- Temporary run progress and permanent unlocks must never overwrite each other.
- Independent Rinnegan handling must not merge with ordinary reward or spin pools.
- Bijuu permanent unlocks are challenge-earned and separate from the 50% Bijuu Mode Card roll behavior.
- Final Part 3 room data and boss specifications remain pending.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Consertar o fluxo para que a partida realmente comece ao selecionar “BEGIN THE RUN”.
- Completar e validar o roguelike 2D inspirado em Naruto.

## Requirements
- Preservar resolução lógica 960×540, shell 16:9, renderização interna 480×270, controles mobile em paisagem e passo fixo de combate.
- Preservar `ashesSave`, progressão permanente separada das cartas temporárias e recompensas exatas de 4/5/6/7/8 cards.
- Uma recompensa por sala elegível, com roteamento de inimigos eliminados via `completeStoryRoom()`.
- Preservar sistemas separados de Rinnegan e Bijuu.
- Manter apresentação pixel-art e validar gameplay em desktop e mobile.

## Decisions
- O clique em “BEGIN THE RUN” deve iniciar diretamente a primeira sala, sem exigir uma etapa modal intermediária.
- Os reinícios devem sempre zerar pausa, modal e estado temporário da corrida.
- `initRun()` agora chama `startStoryRoom()` diretamente após criar o personagem.

## Work State
### Completed
- Corrigida a entrada inicial em `initRun()`: pausa, modais, jogador e primeira sala são reinicializados corretamente.
- O handler de `#start-run` agora cancela o evento e chama `initRun()`.
- Confirmado que `node --check game.js` passa.
- Servidor local foi iniciado em `http://127.0.0.1:4173`.
- Chromium headless conseguiu gerar captura em `/tmp/ashes-start-fixed.png`.

### Active
- Validar em navegador que o mapa/combate continua ativo após o clique e que movimento e ataque funcionam.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Executar teste interativo real no Chromium para confirmar fechamento do menu, início dos inimigos e atualização do combate.
2. Testar movimento, ataque, pulo e controles mobile após o início.
3. Verificar reinício, derrota, vitória e avanço pelas salas/recompensas.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: fluxo de início da corrida, handlers dos botões, combate e roteamento das salas.
- `index.html`: botões do menu, canvas, modal e controles touch.
- `style.css`: apresentação do menu, modais e layout responsivo.
- `/tmp/ashes-start-fixed.png`: captura headless recente usada na validação visual.

## Important Context
- `game.js` e `style.css` possuem alterações não commitadas.
- A alteração mais recente manteve o `#start-run` como início direto e removeu a necessidade de abrir o mapa logo no primeiro clique.
- Ainda falta uma validação interativa completa, pois a tentativa anterior ficou limitada pela indisponibilidade de `playwright` como módulo local no processo Node.
